# Agent notes

This repository is an OpenCode plugin. Read the README for what it does; this file is for working on it.

## Layout and checks

- `src/` is the plugin, `test/` the suites, `scripts/` the checks. `npm run check` runs typecheck, unit, conformance,
  kit, build, icons, host, pack, forbidden, copies, whitelist and actionlint, in that order.
- `npm run check` with `OPENCODE_BIN_2_2_3` to `OPENCODE_BIN_2_2_6` set runs the host and pack stages against every
  tested release; once unset it falls back to the locked SDK with a notice.
- `npm run drift` compares the plugin's tool table with `test/fixtures/live-tools.json`.
- The host suite needs Bun 1.4.4 and Node 24. It starts an embedded OpenCode, so it must not run against a real account:
  the fake server is loopback only, and any fetch that leaves loopback fails the run. On 2.3.1 and later the harness
  builds that host through `PromiseSdk.create`, which `OpenCode.create` calls, with the SDK's `overrides` so that its
  Automation service also runs the scheduler, as `opencode serve` does: Code Mode with nobody present runs there as an
  automation's code action (`unattended` in `test/host/harness.ts`).

## Forbidden in this repository

Checked by `scripts/check-forbidden.mjs` across `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/` and `dist/`:

- fork-only markers (`dispatch-lease`, `catalog-ownership`, text-only response markers), `options.mcp` delegation,
  `Plugin.image`, imported OAuth grants;
- the V1 plugin API (`@opencode-ai/*`), V1 hooks (`tool.execute.before`, `chat.message`, `permission.ask`),
  `ctx.generate.text`, `experimental.policies`, and `@opencode/ai`;
- a permission hook other than the tools RPC's one evaluate hook;
- private host source paths and host checkouts;
- machine-local home and temp paths;
- internal process wording: who decided what, lane names, ticket references of our own.

## House rules

- The tools RPC's transport is source-contract's `tools-rpc` module (`@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract`, a dev
  dependency pinned to a tag and bundled into `dist/index.js`); `src/host/tools-rpc.ts` is ElevenLabs' part of it.
  `test/support/jelly-kit.ts` and `test/support/jelly-settings.ts` are copies every plugin shares: `npm run check`
  fails the copies stage when either differs.
- The source `elevenlabs.conversations` (`src/events.ts`, `package.json`'s `sources`) is metadata only: the callers are
  other people, so an event never carries a caller, a transcript, a summary, a score or feedback, and its `text` stays
  empty. It reads only `agents_list_conversations`, `agents_list` and `agents_get`, all free reads (the last two for
  each agent's retention, which decides its `gap`); every tool it adds must be a free read, `permission.operations`
  must name exactly what it reads, and the conformance stage (`npm run conformance`) fails otherwise.
- The tool table is `src/elevenlabs-tools.ts` and nothing else: the default rules, the tools RPC, status, the spending
  guard, the Jelly declaration and the tests all derive from it.
- Every error the plugin raises has a code from `PLUGIN_CODES`, and the README's and the configuration guide's tables
  must match it exactly.
- The plugin never sees the OAuth token, and never prints one. Anything read from the network goes through
  `src/redact.ts` before it reaches status or the session.
- A tool that writes asserts its own permission inside `execute`; a declared `permission` alone does not ask.
- The tool table and the estimate's shape were measured in live reconcile 1 (`test/fixtures/README.md`): the catalogue
  is the live one, an estimate costs nothing but creates a flow, and its figure is the batch total and may be
  fractional. One fact is still unverified, and the README's Known limits is the one place that says so: whether a paid
  result reports what it really cost, and in which field. Do not state that as settled, and do not call the tool table
  provisional.
- The icon `assets/icon.svg` (and the two PNGs rendered from it) is ElevenLabs' own "11" symbol, the published
  `elevenlabs-symbol.svg` from https://elevenlabs.io/brand in its own 876 canvas: the two black bars exactly as published,
  on a white holding square three times their height, as the brand page asks. `opencode.vendor.mark` is `true`. Do not
  recolour, redraw or combine it, and keep the README's trademark line.
- Releases come only from `.github/workflows/release.yml` ("Releasing" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)). A
  release-prep PR sets `version` in `package.json` and the install specs and runs `node scripts/changelog.mjs release`;
  once it is on `master` and CI passed, start the release with
  `gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f sha=<its full sha>`. The workflow builds `dist/`, makes the release
  commit on a temporary `release/v<version>` branch, checks and stages everything, and waits for the owner to approve
  the `release` environment; only then does it create the tag `v<version>` and the GitHub Release. Never push a tag or a
  `release/*` branch, and never commit, tag or publish a release by hand. Agents never approve a release, never call the
  deployment-approval API, and never bypass a ruleset or the environment.
- No personal email in anything we publish. Every commit is authored and committed as
  `joe-broadhead <91376460+joe-broadhead@users.noreply.github.com>`, except the release commit and tag, which the
  release workflow makes as `github-actions[bot]`. Before committing or tagging, check that
  `git config user.email` is that address: a fresh clone inherits the machine's global identity, which is not that
  address. Never commit, tag or publish with a work or personal address, or with a local hostname.

# ElevenLabs call review

A conversation holds a real person's words, the identifier your integration gave them, the phone number they called from,
whatever the agent was told to extract, and the variables their app passed in. Treat all of it as personal data about
someone who did not choose to talk to a model.

## Reading

- `agents_list_conversations` for the calls themselves: agent, time, duration, outcome. Start here.
- `agents_get_conversation` with a `conversation_id` for one call: the transcript turns, the post-call summary, the
  extracted fields, and `cost` in credits beside `cost_fiat` in dollars.
- `agents_search_conversation_messages` searches the words across calls, and
  `agents_semantic_search_conversation_messages` searches by meaning. Use them when the user remembers what was said,
  not which call it was.
- `agents_get_conversation_summary` gives the post-call summary alone, which is often enough and carries less of the
  caller's own words.
- `agents_get_conversation_audio_url` returns a link to a call's recording that works for 15 minutes. Give the link to
  the user; never fetch it, and never pass it to another tool.
- `agents_query_workspace_conversations` counts calls, minutes and credits across agents, without anyone's words.
- `agents_list_batch_calls` and `agents_get_batch_call` show outbound batches: each recipient's status and the
  `conversation_id` of each call made.

## Reporting

- **Summarise; do not dump.** Quote at most the turns that carry the finding, and say which call and when.
- Never copy a caller's name, number, address or extracted field into another tool, a file, a commit, a message or a public
  page. Keep the call id and let the user open the call.
- Never send transcript text to a web search, a research tool or an external service.
- If the answer needs who the person is, give the call id and the time; the user can open it in the ElevenLabs app.
- An empty result means no call matched within the user's access and the filters used. Say that; do not guess a cause.

## The `conversations` option

The plugin can deny these reads without denying the metadata ones. `conversations: "summary"` denies the five tools
that return a caller's words or voice — `agents_get_conversation`, `agents_get_conversation_summary`,
`agents_search_conversation_messages`, `agents_semantic_search_conversation_messages` and
`agents_get_conversation_audio_url` — and keeps the counts and the listings. `"off"` denies those and every other
conversation read, `agents_list_conversations`, `agents_list_memories`, the triage tickets and the batch calls
included. If a call is refused, the option or a rule stopped it - say so and name the option, and do not try another
route to the same words.

## Cost

A conversation's `cost` is ElevenLabs credits, and `cost_fiat` is dollars. Report credits as credits; the plugin never
converts one to the other.

## Not this skill

The user's own meetings are Granola, Wispr Flow or Plaud. Changing what an agent says is the `elevenlabs` skill.

# ElevenLabs generation

Generations land on a **Flow**, the editable canvas that holds the prompt and the results. They **spend the workspace's
credits**, so read this first. Pass only the arguments a tool's own schema lists.

## What spends

Eighteen tools bill the workspace. On a flow: `creative_generate_speech`, `creative_generate_image`,
`creative_generate_video`, `creative_edit_image`, `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes`,
`creative_transcribe_audio`, `creative_design_voice`, `creative_execute_sandbox` (per second) and
`creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`; everything else on a flow is free. The `elevenlabs` skill covers the other
eight: `agents_submit_batch_call`, `agents_retry_batch_call`, `agents_run_tests`, `agents_run_attached_tests`, `agents_generate`,
`agents_generate_test_from_conversation`, `agents_compute_kb_rag_index` and `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag`.

## Pricing

- **Price first only when the user asks what something will cost.** ElevenLabs is the only source of a price; there
  is no rate card to work from. Send the same call with `estimate_only: true` and read the figure that comes back:

  ```json
  { "prompt": "a ceramic mug on marble, morning light", "model_id": "gpt-image-2", "generations_count": 1, "estimate_only": true }
  ```

  ```js
  const priced = await tools.elevenlabs.creative_generate_image({ prompt, model_id: "gpt-image-2", generations_count: 1, estimate_only: true })
  ```

  Say the price and what it buys, then make the paid call with the same arguments. An estimate charges nothing, but it
  does create a flow and a node in the workspace, so do not price a call the user did not ask to have priced, and ask
  for one estimate per set of arguments, not per attempt.
- **The figure is for the whole batch**, not for one generation, and it can be fractional.
- **Every paid result carries a cost line.** It states what the result itself reported, such as
  `Credits: 762; 762 credits today.`, or `Credits: not reported; …` when the result reported nothing. Repeat it as it
  is; never turn an estimate or a guess into a charge.
- `generations_count` defaults to **4** for image, video and image editing, and to **2** for speech. Pass `1` unless the
  user asked for options.
- `creative_design_voice` and `agents_run_tests` take no `estimate_only`, so nothing can price them, even on request.
  Say so before calling one, and report the cost line their result carries.
- **Never call a generating tool twice to "retry".** A retry starts and charges a second generation. Poll
  `creative_get_flow_run_status` with the `flow_id` until it reports `all_completed` or `has_failures`.
- The workspace's own credit balance at ElevenLabs is the limit. If the user set a credit cap in this plugin's options,
  a call over it is refused with `SPEND_CAP_REACHED` or `PRICE_UNKNOWN`; pass the refusal's next step on rather than
  working around it.

## Speech

`creative_generate_speech` puts the spoken words in `prompt` — there is no `text` parameter — and needs a `voice_id`
and a `model_id`. Call `creative_list_voices` first; a `voice_id` only ever comes from there or from the user. The
default model is `eleven_multilingual_v2`, or `eleven_v3` when the script has audio tags such as `[whispering]`.
Speech returns two takes by default and each is charged.

## Images and video

`creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video` and `creative_edit_image` take `prompt` and `model_id`;
`creative_edit_image` also takes `connect_from`, a node on the same flow. `gemini-2.5-flash-image` is the general
default; `gpt-image-2` for rendered text, infographics and reference-driven edits; `flux-2-pro` for fine detail.
`creative_get_model_guide` explains how to prompt one model, `creative_get_model_schema` gives its parameters, and
`creative_get_flow_node_types` lists what the workspace can run.

## Chaining on one flow

Nodes on different flows cannot be connected. Call `creative_create_flow` first, then pass that `flow_id` to every
related call and wire with `connect_from` (a `node_id` from a tool result or `creative_get_flow`, never invented).
`creative_generate_in_flow` adds and runs a node of a given `node_type`; `creative_run_flow_nodes` re-runs the
`node_ids` you name. Both are charged like any other generation.

## Keeping a file

A result carries a signed link on `elevenlabsusercontent.com` that **expires in about two hours**, plus a canvas `url`
that does not. To keep the file, call `elevenlabs_save_media` with the link:

```json
{ "url": "https://…elevenlabsusercontent.com/…", "name": "intro-voiceover.mp3" }
```

It answers with the path, size, sha256 and, when the container states one, the duration. Files go under the plugin's
`mediaRoot` (status shows it; the default is `~/Downloads/elevenlabs`). Never paste the bytes into the conversation, never
put a generated file in a git repository unless the user asks, and never re-generate to "refresh" an expired link: fetch
the generation again, or open the flow.

## Transcription

`creative_transcribe_audio` transcribes a node already on a flow: it takes `connect_from` and a `model_id`, never a file
or a path from this machine. To transcribe audio that is not on a flow yet, put it there first with
`creative_create_asset_upload` and `creative_finalize_asset_upload`, and say that the audio leaves the machine before
doing it. The transcription itself is charged like a generation.

## Not this skill

Agent settings are the `elevenlabs` skill. What callers said to an agent is `elevenlabs-calls`.

# ElevenLabs agents

Read this before the first `agents_*` call. Pass only the arguments a tool's own schema lists.

## Start by reading

`agents_list` to find the agent, then `agents_get` for its configuration. Ids only ever come from a tool result or the
user; never guess or rebuild one. `agents_get` is a read and runs freely:

```js
const found = await tools.elevenlabs.agents_list({ search: "checkout" })
const agent = await tools.elevenlabs.agents_get({ agent_id: found[0].agent_id })
```

## Changing an agent

`agents_update` **publishes to the live branch immediately**, `main` by default. It is not a draft and this plugin cannot
undo it. So:

- read the agent first, and send only the fields that should change;
- say what will change and that it goes live, in one sentence;
- for anything a caller could notice, prefer `agents_create_branch`, make the change on the branch, then
  `agents_merge_branch_preview` before `agents_merge_branch`.

`agents_duplicate` is usually better than rebuilding a configuration by hand.

Workflow, attachment and test edits (`agents_add_workflow_node`, `agents_attach_tool`, `agents_duplicate_test` and the
like) are staged in your own draft of a branch, not live. `agents_publish_draft` **makes every staged change live to
callers at once**: say what goes live and on which branch, in one sentence, before calling it.

## Calls, numbers and people

These reach people outside this conversation. Confirm with the user first, every time, and make the one call:

- `agents_submit_batch_call` **places real phone calls** to every recipient in the list, now or at the scheduled time,
  and spends credits. Read the recipients back to the user and get a yes before calling it. `agents_retry_batch_call`
  calls the failed and unanswered recipients again, and spends again. `agents_cancel_batch_call` stops the recipients
  not yet called. `agents_list_batch_calls` and `agents_get_batch_call` report what happened.
- `agents_update_whatsapp_account` changes how an agent answers a WhatsApp number's users.
- `agents_request_merge_proposal_review` notifies the workspace members named.
- `agents_create_phone_number`, `agents_create_secret` and `agents_update_secret` store credentials that are never
  returned. Take a value only from the user, and never repeat it.

## Knowledge base

Add with `agents_create_kb_url` (a page that can keep syncing) or `agents_create_kb_text`; organise with
`agents_create_kb_folder`. Before a delete, check `agents_get_kb_dependents`: other agents may use the document.
`agents_bulk_delete_knowledge_base` is irreversible.

## Tests and deployment

Create a test with `agents_create_test`; inspect past runs with `agents_list_test_runs` and `agents_get_test_run`.
`agents_run_tests` and `agents_run_attached_tests` **spend credits**: they make the agent hold conversations, and
ElevenLabs offers no estimate for them, so say so before running one and report the cost line its result carries.
`agents_generate` (an LLM writes a whole agent) and `agents_generate_test_from_conversation` are counted as spending too. A deployment moves live traffic:
`agents_create_deployment` after a merge, not before.

## Cost

Before a change that switches the model, `agents_calculate_llm_usage` reports what a conversation would cost. Say the
figure and its basis when the user is choosing.

## Deletes

`agents_delete`, `agents_delete_tool`, `agents_delete_phone_number` and `agents_bulk_delete_knowledge_base` cannot be
undone. Say what will be deleted and whom it affects, in one sentence, then make the one call: the plugin asks for
permission at `access: "ask-changes"` and refuses it at `"read-only"`. If the call is declined, nothing changed.

## Not this skill

Call history and transcripts are `elevenlabs-calls`. Generation is `elevenlabs-creative`.

# ElevenLabs for OpenCode

Manage the voice and chat agents in your ElevenLabs workspace, review what callers said to them, and generate speech,
images and video through ElevenLabs' official MCP server, from OpenCode.

Unofficial; not affiliated with ElevenLabs.

ElevenLabs is a trademark of Eleven Labs Inc.; this unofficial plugin is not endorsed by them.

## Requirements

- OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`. Tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2.
- macOS or Linux.
- An ElevenLabs account with a workspace. Generations spend that workspace's credits.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.9
```

Run `opencode reload`, or restart OpenCode, then run `/elevenlabs-status`.

Each release has its own tag, and a Git install does not update by itself. To move to a newer release, remove the old entry with `opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.8`, then add the new tag with `opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<version>`.

Or add the plugin to `opencode.json` instead, with the same spec:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.9" }] }
```

The install takes the GitHub release tag. Its commit carries the built `dist/`, so the install runs no build.
A new release is a new tag: install it with its own `#v<version>` spec.

## Sign in

Run `/connect` and choose **ElevenLabs**. In the terminal, press `o` or Enter to open the link; on the command line,
`opencode mcp auth elevenlabs` opens the browser itself and `opencode auth login elevenlabs` does the same. Sign in with
your account, choose the workspace, and approve the permissions the consent screen lists.

No API key is copied anywhere, and no client ID ships with the plugin: ElevenLabs accepts a client metadata document, so
OpenCode registers itself with the consent screen. Revoke the connection at any time from OpenCode, or from your
ElevenLabs account settings.

The consent is for seven scopes: `convai_read`, `convai_write`, `text_to_speech`, `speech_history_read`, `flows`,
`image_video_generation` and `voice_generation`. ElevenLabs also advertises `ads_read`; this plugin never asks for it,
because it has no advertising tool.

## Use

Ask for what you want in your own words:

- "List my agents and tell me which ones still use the default first message."
- "My checkout agent fails when someone asks about refunds. Read yesterday's calls and tell me why."
- "Duplicate the production agent, change the voice, and set the first message to Spanish."
- "Price a five-second video of a ceramic mug in morning light, tell me what it costs, then make it."
- "Save that voiceover to my Downloads folder."

One tool and one guard do more than relay ElevenLabs:

- **`elevenlabs_save_media`** writes a generated file to disk from the signed link a generation returns. The link expires
  about two hours after the generation, so this is how a result is kept. It answers with the path, size, sha256 and, when
  the file states one, the duration; the file itself never enters the conversation.
- **a spending guard** adds a cost line to every paid result. It prices a call first and refuses one that does not fit
  only when you set a credit cap.

A script can call the same tools with no model, under the same spending guard:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/agents_list -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{}}}'
```

[docs/scripting.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs/blob/HEAD/docs/scripting.md) has the envelope,
the estimate path and every refusal.

### The conversations source

The plugin declares one [source contract](https://github.com/we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract) source,
`elevenlabs.conversations`, so a collector such as Memory or a dashboard can read the workspace's calls without the
model. `elevenlabs_events_list` (a tool, and an `events_list` method of the RPC above) lists the conversations the
workspace's agents had since a cursor, oldest first, and `probe` names the sign-in.

Each event is metadata only, because the callers are other people: the conversation's id, its start, the agent as its
one actor, and a title of the agent's name with the call's direction, status and outcome, such as
`Support Desk: inbound call, done, successful`. No caller's name or number, no transcript, summary, score or feedback,
and no link. A conversation is listed once it is done or failed, or two hours after it started. Reading goes through
three free reads only, so it spends no credits: `agents_list_conversations`, and, when a read starts more than a day
back, `agents_list` and `agents_get` for each agent's retention. `conversations: "off"` turns it off. ElevenLabs names
no account, so the owner is OpenCode's sign-in for ElevenLabs. `npm run conformance` runs the contract's kit offline
and writes the report each release carries.

ElevenLabs deletes an agent's conversations after its retention period, two years unless it is changed. A read that
starts before the latest of those horizons answers `gap` (`expired`) once, then lists what survives. **An agent with
retention 0, or in Zero Retention Mode, keeps no conversations: the source never sees its calls, and answers no gap for
them.** Known limits below has the rest.

`/elevenlabs-status` prints the connection, the account, the region, the spend, the tools and one next step.
`/elevenlabs` opens the same report in a dialog. `/elevenlabs-doctor` makes the live checks a status report cannot.

## Spending

Generations are billed in **credits** against the workspace you signed in with.

- **There is no credit cap unless you set one.** ElevenLabs already refuses a call the workspace's balance cannot pay
  for, and the permission rules decide whether a paid call runs at all: under `access: "ask-changes"` every generation
  asks, and under `"read-only"` it is denied. With the default options the plugin refuses, cuts and queues nothing for
  money and sends no estimate before a paid call. Each paid result's cost line says what the result reported, or
  `Credits: not reported`; it never shows a guess. To know a price first, ask for it: an `estimate_only` call.
- **Caps are opt-in.** Set `sessionCreditCap`, `dailyCreditCap` or both to a whole number of credits to add a bound of
  your own, counted over a rolling 24 hours across sessions, scripts and restarts. While either is set, a generation
  that does not fit is refused **before it is sent**, a request for more variations than the budget affords is cut to
  what fits, and the rest of this section's refusals apply.
- **How far a cap reaches.** Every hold and every charge is written to this data directory's store under its own key,
  which only the OpenCode that created it ever rewrites, and a total is read by scanning those keys and adding them up.
  Nothing merges two writers' records, so no writer can drop another's charge. What a cap cannot do is decide across two
  running OpenCodes at once: `ctx.storage` has no compare-and-set and no lock, so each admits a call against what it has
  read. Exactly: **within one OpenCode the caps are exact; across OpenCodes a cap is crossed by at most one call's
  reservation for each one deciding before its read of the others' holds lands, so eight of them at 3,000 credits a
  call can spend 31,000 against a 10,000 cap; every OpenCode reads the store behind each call it admits and every five
  seconds besides, so none decides on a book older than that; a settled charge is never lost.** The crossing needs
  overlap: calls that wait for one another see one another, and those same eight, run one after the next, spend only
  the 9,000 that fits. Size a cap as the bound you can afford to be crossed once per extra OpenCode, not as a hard
  limit on the account. Two machines share nothing: the store cannot see them.
- **Every price comes from ElevenLabs, never from this plugin.** There is no rate table here: no credits per character,
  per second or per minute, and nothing measures a file on this machine. A price is ElevenLabs' answer to the **same
  call with `estimate_only: true`**: you or the model can ask for one at any time, and while a cap is set the plugin
  asks for one itself before each paid call. Eighteen tools can spend:
  `creative_generate_speech`, `creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video`, `creative_edit_image`,
  `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes`, `creative_transcribe_audio`, `creative_design_voice`,
  `creative_execute_sandbox`, `agents_submit_batch_call`, `agents_retry_batch_call`, `agents_run_tests`,
  `agents_run_attached_tests`, `agents_generate`, `agents_generate_test_from_conversation`,
  `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`. The
  first seven take `estimate_only`; the other eleven do not, so they run unpriced, and while a cap you set is on they
  are refused instead. The sandbox says it bills by the second, and the two batch-call tools place real phone calls.
  The rest are counted as spending because ElevenLabs' catalogue says neither way and the work they describe — a test
  run's conversations, an LLM writing an agent or a test, embedding a document, running a RAG query, reading a website
  — is work it plausibly bills, so each gets a cost line and, under a cap, counts against it.
- **An estimate is free, but it is not nothing.** Measured against a real workspace: two estimates moved the balance by
  zero credits, and each left a flow and a node behind in the workspace. That is why none is sent without a cap. Under a
  cap, one estimate is asked per set of arguments,
  the figure is kept for ten minutes, and the paid call reuses it instead of creating a second flow. The estimate is
  sent only where the paid call could run: the permission it asks for is the generation's own, so nothing is estimated
  if you say no, and under `access: "read-only"` every spending tool is denied and no estimate is sent either. The
  plugin raises that permission twice for one paid call — before the estimate, and again for the generation — so under
  `ask-changes` you may be prompted twice. Whether OpenCode folds the two into one prompt is OpenCode's to decide, and
  no release has measured it yet.
- **The figure is the whole batch.** ElevenLabs answers for every generation the call asks for, not for one — a
  four-image estimate came back as 761.5151418103446 credits, about 190 an image. Credits are charged as whole numbers,
  so a fractional figure is rounded up. Under a cap, a batch that does not fit is cut to the number of generations the
  budget affords, and a call that named no count is refused whole rather than quietly given a smaller batch.
- **With no cap, nothing is priced first and nothing is refused.** A cost line reads `Credits: not reported` unless the
  result reports a figure. **With a cap, a call that cannot be priced is refused, not guessed.** Only when you set a cap: each of the 18 tools that can spend is priced by ElevenLabs' own estimate or refused PRICE_UNKNOWN before it is sent, and so is any name this table does not classify, whatever it starts with. With no cap, the default, nothing is refused for want of a price.
  A failed or missing estimate, an argument ElevenLabs' own schema for that tool does not have, and a tool with no
  estimate at all each end there. The refusal says what to do: send the same call with `estimate_only: true`, or set
  both caps to `null`. A price of 0 is a refusal, not a free call.
- **Transcription spends like everything else.** `creative_transcribe_audio` transcribes a node on a flow — it takes no
  file and no path — and it is priced from its own estimate. It is **not** a read: `access: "read-only"` denies it along
  with every other tool that can spend.
- **Under a cap, two calls that start together cannot both spend the same budget.** The price is reserved in the ledger
  before the call is sent and settled when its result arrives. A call that fails, or whose result never arrives, is
  charged the reserved price: the plugin cannot tell a free failure from a billed one, and over-counting is the safe
  side. A later result that reports a higher figure may replace that charge. A missing result, a zero, or an error does
  not free the budget. A hold still open after ten minutes is settled at the reserved price rather than dropped. On the
  script path, one priced call per session and method is in flight; a second is refused until the first settles. With
  no cap none of this holds anything back: calls run side by side and each is recorded when its result arrives.
- **Past a thousand priced calls in a day, the oldest ones are counted by the hour.** The detail log keeps the newest
  1,000 charges; an older charge still inside the window is folded into a total for its session and the hour it was
  spent in, which nothing afterwards can shrink. A folded total is kept while any minute of its hour is still inside the
  24 hours, so a folded charge can go on counting for up to an hour after its own day ran out. The total errs high,
  never low, and only on a day that busy.
- **A cap bounds this plugin, not your account.** Someone generating in the ElevenLabs app spends from the same pool,
  and so does a second MCP entry pointing at ElevenLabs under another name: its tools carry that name's prefix, which
  this plugin's guard never sees. `/elevenlabs-status` names such an entry when it finds one.
- **The balance is only visible with an API key.** Add one through `/connect` → **ElevenLabs API key (optional, balance only)** and
  status shows the workspace balance and its reset date. It is used for one read, the subscription, and never to
  generate. Without it the Spend row says the plugin counts its own calls only.
- **A retry is a second charge.** The skills poll for a result instead of asking again.
- **No dollar figure is derived from credits.** There is no published conversion; `cost_fiat`, when ElevenLabs reports
  it, is the dollars.

## Media and files

Generated files are saved under `mediaRoot`, default `~/Downloads/elevenlabs`, created on the first save with mode 0700.
Only a link on ElevenLabs' generated-file host is fetched, over `https`, with no redirect to any other host, and a file
larger than `maxMediaBytes` (200 MB by default) is refused.

That folder is outside your project, so **two rules apply**: the plugin's own permission, and OpenCode's
`external_directory` rule for the folder. The plugin asserts both before it fetches anything, and its refusal prints the
exact rule. To pre-approve the folder:

```json
{ "permissions": [
  { "action": "elevenlabs_save_media", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
  { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "/absolute/path/of/your/mediaRoot/*", "effect": "allow" }
] }
```

The second resource is the **absolute** path of `mediaRoot` followed by `/*`; a `~` is not expanded in a rule, so write
the path out (`/absolute/path/...`, not `~/...`). A refusal that starts `permission.rejected: external_directory` or
`EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY_DENIED` needs that second rule.

## Regions

ElevenLabs runs separate environments, and an isolated one is a separate workspace with a separate account.

| `region` | Server |
| --- | --- |
| `global` (the default) | `https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp` |
| `us` | `https://api.us.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp` |
| `eu` | `https://api.eu.residency.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp` |
| `in` | `https://api.in.residency.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp` |
| `sg` | `https://api.sg.residency.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp` |

The server address is part of the stored credential's key, so **changing `region` needs a new sign-in**: run `/connect`

in OpenCode, unused. A plugin cannot delete a stored credential, so this one does the rest: it lists the old sign-in in

names it with the command that removes it, `opencode auth logout <its id>`. If your own `mcp.servers.elevenlabs` entry
still points at the old region, status says so and gives one next step.

## Known limits

- **Stop does not cancel a price estimate already sent.** While a credit cap is on, the estimate runs in OpenCode's
  `execute.before` hook, which is given no signal, so it finishes even when the call it prices is stopped.
- **The tool table is the live catalogue.** It was captured from a signed-in workspace on 14 November 2026: 237 tools,
  with each one's real argument names, defaults, enums and ElevenLabs' own read-only marks, kept in
  `test/fixtures/live-tools.json` and checked by `npm run drift` and the unit tests. A tool ElevenLabs adds after that
  capture still runs, under the `elevenlabs_*` rule, and `/elevenlabs-status` names it as unknown until it is
  classified.
- **ElevenLabs no longer takes a `context` argument.** Earlier releases told the model to pass one; the live schemas
  have none, and under a cap a priced call that carries it is refused as an unknown argument.
- **There is no credit cap by default.** The workspace's balance at ElevenLabs and the permission rules are the bounds;
  a cap you set bounds this plugin, not the account. The workspace balance is visible with the optional API key.
- **No dollar figure is derived from credits.**
- **With no cap, a cost line is only as good as the result.** No estimate is sent before a paid call, so a result that
  reports no figure says `Credits: not reported`. Under a cap you set, prices come from ElevenLabs' own estimate: a
  call it cannot price is refused rather than guessed, and a tool ElevenLabs offers no estimate for cannot run.
- **One fact about a paid call stays unverified until the live reconcile measures it:** whether a finished generation
  reports what it really cost, and in which field of its result. Pass 1 did not measure it: it spent nothing. Pass 2
  does, as step 2 of the checklist in `test/fixtures/README.md`, on the two cheapest paid calls this plugin can make.
  Until then a call under a cap is recorded at its estimate, and a later figure can only raise that charge, never lower
  it; with no cap, most cost lines may read `Credits: not reported`. What the live pass did settle is on the
  estimate's side: an estimate moved the balance by nothing, its figure covers the whole batch rather than one
  generation, it can be fractional, and it leaves a flow and a node behind in the workspace.
- **Durations are read from the container, and only for display.** WAV and MP4/M4A state one; MP3, Ogg and WebM do not,
  and the field is left out rather than estimated. A WAV holding more than one `data` chunk, or more than one `fmt `
  chunk, states two durations, and real decoders disagree about which counts, so it is treated as stating none. No
  price reads any of this.

- **A region change cannot remove the earlier region's sign-in.** A plugin cannot delete a stored credential, so it
  stays in OpenCode until you sign out of it: `/connect` lists it as "ElevenLabs, old `<region>` sign-in (not in use)",
  and `/elevenlabs-status` gives the `opencode auth logout` command.
- **Jelly's relay sign-in is not yet checked with ElevenLabs.** The declaration lets Jelly offer a browser tab its
  relay for the sign-in, which relies on ElevenLabs accepting Jelly's client metadata document; no sign-in through
  that path has been made yet. Signing in from OpenCode itself is unaffected.
- In Jelly, the settings are drawn as choices and bounded numbers, which needs a Jelly that reads them: an older Jelly
  refuses the plugin's whole declaration. Jelly saves no `null`, so a credit cap there is no cap by being left unset.
- **The conversations source sees only what ElevenLabs still lists.**
  - **Retention.** ElevenLabs' docs disagree on whether an agent's retention removes a conversation from the list or
    only its transcript and audio: the [retention page](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/customization/privacy/retention) says "transcripts and audio recordings", the
    [API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/agents/get) says `retention_days` is "the number of days to retain the conversation". The source takes the
    conservative reading, that the conversation goes, and answers a `gap` for a read that starts before the latest
    retention horizon among the agents. An agent that states no retention is taken at the two-year default.
  - **One gap per read, for an hour.** A read that pages on within an hour of its gap answers no second one, so during
    one continuous read up to an hour's worth of conversations at the horizon's edge can be deleted without a second
    gap. A cursor used more than an hour after its gap is a new read: the horizon is checked again, and a pause never
    hides what retention deleted.
  - **Loss by design.** An agent with retention 0, or in Zero Retention Mode, keeps no conversations (ElevenLabs offers
    them only to a post-call webhook). The source never sees them and answers no gap for them.
  - **Deletions.** A conversation a person deletes, or one a shortened retention removes at once, cannot be told apart
    from one that never happened: ElevenLabs offers no list of deletions. One deleted before it was listed is never
    seen; one deleted after it was listed stays with the consumer. Answering that with `removals[]` needs consumers on
    source-contract 0.2.0, and is not sent yet.
  - **A deleted agent** cannot be read, so its retention is not part of the horizon.
  - **Status.** A conversation still running or processing two hours after its start is listed with that status, and
    never listed again when it finishes.
  - **The owner is OpenCode's sign-in,** because ElevenLabs names no account: signing in again, even as the same
    workspace, is a new owner, and a cursor from before it is refused. The owner will carry `verified: false`, and the
    descriptor an empty `permission.identity`, once Memory and jelly are on source-contract 0.2.0; consumers on 0.1.x
    refuse both.
  - **No consent sentence.** The descriptor carries no `scope.describe` for the loss by design above: a descriptor whose
    `scope` names no keys is refused by the contract's own descriptor schema, so this README and the tool's description
    say it instead.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## Uninstall

Sign out first, so the stored credential goes with the plugin. If `/elevenlabs-status` names a sign-in left from an
earlier region, run the `opencode auth logout` command it gives as well:

```sh
opencode mcp logout elevenlabs
opencode auth list
opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.9
```

Files already saved under `mediaRoot` stay. Remove them yourself if you no longer want them.

## What live reconcile 1 measured

The first signed-in pass settled the catalogue and the shape of a price. It did not spend: every call it made was a
read or an estimate.

- **The catalogue**: 190 tools (144 `agents_*`, 45 `creative_*`, and `get_more_tools`). `creative_generate_music`,
  `creative_compose_music` and `creative_generate_sound_effect` are not among them. Exactly 7 tools accept
  `estimate_only`.
- **Every tool required `context`** then, a short line naming the reason for the call. None does since.
- **An estimate looked free.** Two `estimate_only: true` calls, with the workspace balance read before and after each
  (`GET /v1/user/subscription`), moved it by nothing, and no new billable request appeared.
- **An estimate is not free of effects**: each one created a flow and a node in the workspace. That is why the guard
  asks for one estimate per set of arguments and remembers it for ten minutes.
- **The figure is the batch total, and it can be fractional.** `creative_generate_image` with `generations_count: 4`
  answered `761.5151418103446` credits — about 190 an image — beside `price_cents`, `generations_count`, `currency`,
  `estimated_runtime_seconds`, `flow_id`, `flow_created`, `node_id` and `url`.
- **`creative_transcribe_audio` takes no file and no path.** Its arguments are `connect_from`, `flow_id`, `model_id`,
  `view_state_id`, `context` and `estimate_only` then (no `context` now): it transcribes a node on a flow, so no local file can be part of a
  price.

## The live checklist for reconcile 2

The eight things the deep review of the estimate-first reconcile left for a signed-in session, in review order. One
session, both caps left on, and the workspace balance (`GET /v1/user/subscription`) read immediately before and after
every step — the movement is the measurement, not what any result claims.

Each step carries the most it may cost. **The whole list is budgeted at 850 credits.** Four of its eight steps are
budgeted at nothing at all, and step 7 is expected to cost nothing but carries a margin in case it does: that
expectation is itself one of the things being tested. If a step moves the balance by more than its maximum, stop there
and record what happened rather than running the rest; a step that overruns has already answered a question the plugin
was deciding from an assumption.

| # | Step | Expected maximum |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The estimate result in full | 0 |
| 2 | What a finished generation reports as its cost | 200 |
| 3 | Do the three newly-classed tools bill? | 300 |
| 4 | Prompts raised by one priced generation | 0 |
| 5 | `get_more_tools`, sent once | 0 |
| 6 | The two tools that take no estimate | 300 |
| 7 | Does `creative_show_flow_results` do anything but render? | 50 |
| 8 | The catalogue count and the full name list | 0 |
| | **Total** | **850** |

1. **The estimate result in full — 0 credits.** Send `estimate_only: true` for at least `creative_generate_speech` and
   `creative_generate_image`, and save the whole result: `output` and every `content` block, verbatim. Two questions
   settle `estimatedCreditsOf`, which now reads `estimate.credits` and five attested keys at the top level and
   nothing else: whether any text block echoes the caller's own prompt back, and whether a credit-shaped key appears
   anywhere other than `estimate.credits`. Pass 1 measured an estimate as free; if either of these two moves the
   balance, that is the finding and the rest of the list waits.
2. **What a finished generation reports as its real cost, and in which field — 200 credits.** The one unverified fact
   in the whole plugin, and `README.md`'s **Known limits** is the only place that says so: *"whether a finished
   generation reports what it really cost, and in which field"*. Two paid calls answer it. The smallest real speech
   generation: `creative_list_voices` for a `voice_id`, then `creative_generate_speech` with `generations_count: 1`, a
   `model_id` of `eleven_multilingual_v2` and a prompt of one short sentence — the estimate first, then the same
   arguments without the flag (**under 100**). Then the smallest real transcription: a few seconds of audio on a flow
   (`creative_create_asset_upload`, then `creative_finalize_asset_upload`), then `creative_transcribe_audio` with
   `connect_from` set to that node, estimate first (**under 100**). For each, record every field of the paid result
   beside the balance movement. If a field carries the real figure, `settlementOf` can settle on it and that README
   bullet is replaced by a measurement; until then a call is charged what it reserved and a later figure may only
   raise it. The same two pairs answer whether the estimate is exact — if a paid call costs less than its estimate,
   the cost line's `basis` must stop saying `"exact"`.
3. **Whether `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and
   `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website` move the balance — 300 credits.** One small call to each, balance either
   side: a RAG index over a single short document, one query against it, one brand kit from one plain site. All three
   were classed as spending on a stated rule — a tool whose description says it does server-side work ElevenLabs
   plausibly bills, and does not say it spends nothing, counts as spending — and none declares `estimate_only`, so
   each is refused outright while a cap is on. This settles that either way: if a tool does not bill, the table
   over-refuses it and `src/elevenlabs-tools.ts` should say so with the measurement beside it.
4. **How many permission prompts one priced generation raises under `access: "ask-changes"` — 0 credits.** One or
   two, counted on step 2's speech generation rather than on a call of its own. The plugin raises one assert, for the
   generation's own action, before it estimates; OpenCode raises the second when the generation runs. Whether the host
   folds them into a single prompt has never been measured, and four documents said "asked once" until this round
   corrected them. Whatever is seen, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/architecture.md`
   are made to say it.
5. **`get_more_tools`, sent once — 0 credits.** One call with a capability sentence, and then `ctx.tool.list()`: what
   comes back, and whether a single new tool is in the list afterwards. The plugin describes it as a free-text channel
   to ElevenLabs that is allowed by default and classifies it as a write; that description is reasoned, not measured,
   and this replaces it with a measured one. Watch the balance anyway: it is the one tool whose effect is unknown.
6. **Whether `creative_design_voice` and `agents_run_tests` really bill, and how much — 300 credits.** First check
   whether either has gained an `estimate_only` argument since pass 1. If not, measure the cheapest run each allows by
   balance movement: three voice previews, one agent test. Both are refused today while a cap is on, because neither
   can be priced before it runs. If either does not bill, the table over-refuses it and should say so.
7. **Whether `creative_show_flow_results` has any billable or workspace effect at all — 50 credits.** It is a read,
   as ElevenLabs marks it: it renders a run's generations back to the user and says it changes nothing. Call it on a
   flow from step 2 and look for both: a balance movement, and any new flow, node or asset in the workspace. If either
   moves, it is not a read, and the table and the declaration keep it stricter with that measurement as the reason.
8. **The catalogue count and the full name list again — 0 credits.** Re-capture `live-tools.json` as Reconciling says

   arguing it.

### Carried from pass 1's list, both free

9. **The argument names — 0 credits.** With step 8's schemas in hand,

   has and the list does not refuses an ordinary call while a cap is on; a name that changes the bill and is on the

10. **`external_directory` — 0 credits.** Whether OpenCode asks for it on a plugin tool that writes with `node:fs`;

1. Capture the list again with the family's capture script against a signed-in OpenCode (`initialize` and

2. `npm run drift` names every tool the plugin does not classify, every tool the list no longer has, and every

## Releasing

Each release is the GitHub tag `v<version>`, where `<version>` is the `version` in `package.json`, and users install from
that tag. The release is one commit on top of a `master` head that CI passed, and the tag points at it. The release
workflow makes both, in GitHub Actions: nobody builds, commits or tags a release on their own machine, and no personal
key signs it.

While changes land, their notes go under `## [Unreleased]` at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`. Each earlier GitHub release is
a `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading below it, newest first, and the npm history stays last, under
`## Earlier releases on npm`.

1. On `master`, set `version` in `package.json` to the new version, and change every install spec in the README,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` to `#v<version>` (`test/docs.test.ts` fails until they match). Then run
   `node scripts/changelog.mjs release`: it turns `## [Unreleased]` into `## [<version>] - <today>`, above the earlier
   releases, and refuses a CHANGELOG it cannot shape. Run `npm run check`.
2. Push that commit to `master`, and wait for CI to pass on it. A pull request's CI runs the Linux runners only; the
   push to `master` runs every runner, Apple-silicon macOS (`macos-26`) too, and the release stands on that run. An
   Intel Mac (`macos-26-intel`) is not required.
3. Start the release with that commit's full sha:
   `gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f sha=<full sha>`, or from Actions → release →
   Run workflow, on `master`.
4. Read the run's summary, then approve the `release` environment. The summary is on the run page, under the `stage`
   job: the tag, the parent and its CI run, the release commit and its tree, the sha256 of `SHA256SUMS` and the staged
   artifact's id, `SHA256SUMS` itself, and the notes. Open the release commit on `release/v<version>` and read them
   before approving: the approval releases exactly those bytes. Only the owner approves a release. Agents never approve
   one, never call the deployment-approval API, and never bypass a ruleset or the environment; the kit's scripts make
   only their own GitHub calls and refuse every other.
5. Check the published Release: not a draft, its notes, and every asset against `SHA256SUMS`.

`package.json` stays `"private": true`, so npm can never publish the plugin by accident; a GitHub install does not read
it, and `npm pack` still packs the release tarball. It is kept in its canonical form, `JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2)` and
one newline: the kit tests check both in `npm run check`, as the release planner does.

The declaration is checked against what the provider serves. `npm run capture` (`scripts/capture-tools.mjs`, run by hand
through the signed-in OpenCode, never by CI) writes `test/fixtures/live-tools.json` and `test/fixtures/provenance.json`,
with the signed-in account's own values that some servers write into descriptions (Slack's "Your user_id: …") replaced
by placeholders such as `U00CURRENTUSER`; the drift check fails a committed capture that still holds one.
`scripts/check-drift.mjs` checks `jelly.tools`, `test/fixtures/tool-registry.json`, the skills and the docs against them,
offline, in the kit tests of `npm run check`. The release build runs it with `--release`, which also refuses a capture
more than 14 days old, unless `provenance.json` holds the owner's written waiver for exactly that capture:
`"waiver": { "listedAt": "<the capture's date>", "reason": "…", "approvedBy": "…" }` (a new capture drops it). A plugin
with no capture yet, or only a names-only one, releases with a warning on the run; one that serves only its own tools
says so with `"upstream": "none"` in the registry.

A plugin that declares sources (a top-level `sources` key in `package.json`, the source contract's declaration) releases
with its conformance report. Its `npm run conformance` runs the source contract's conformance kit and writes
`reports/conformance-report.json` (keep `reports/` out of git); `npm run check` runs it too. The release runs it again on
the parent in its own `conformance` job, which has no write token, and stops unless the run passes and the report's `ok`
is `true` for this version. The report becomes the Release asset `conformance-report.json`, listed in `SHA256SUMS`. A
plugin without `sources` has no report, and its release is unchanged.

Before the approval, the workflow:
- **plans:** refuses a run that is not on `master`, a sha that is not `master`'s head, a sha without a successful
  `ci.yml` push run with a successful job on every runner its push matrix names (macOS included), a `ci.yml` whose
  matrix runs macOS on a pull request or not on a push (the kit tests check it too), a version that is not `x.y.z`, a
  `package.json` that is not `"private": true` or not in its canonical form, a CHANGELOG whose newest release is not
  this version, a plugin that declares sources with no `conformance` script, a release that does not move forward from
  the last published Release, a leftover `release/v<version>` branch, a native run that did not build this sha on
  `master`, by hand, with success, and a missing `native_run` (or one given to a plugin that is not native);
- **builds**: refuses a failing tool drift check (`scripts/check-drift.mjs --release`, above), then builds `dist/` with
  `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run build`, with a read-only token, and writes the release files: `dist/`,
  `package.json` without its lifecycle scripts, and the vetted native manifest;
- **commits** them on a temporary branch `release/v<version>` at the parent, through GitHub's API with the workflow's token,
  so GitHub signs the commit (author `github-actions[bot]`, committer GitHub). This job runs no npm. It refuses a commit
  that GitHub does not verify, or whose parent or tree is not the one the files give;
- **verifies** on a fresh runner: the commit's identity, one parent on `master`, `package.json` exactly the parent's
  without the lifecycle scripts, only regular files in the allowed paths, no `package.json` under `dist/`, and a second,
  independent build of the parent (its own job) equal to the committed `dist/` byte for byte;
- **installs** the release commit with `plugin add` on each stock OpenCode host (2.2.3 to 2.3.2);
- **packs** the commit before installing anything, keeps that tarball and records its sha256, then runs the pack stage
  against a copy;
- **runs the conformance kit** on the parent, for a plugin that declares sources (above), and uploads only its report;
- **stages** the Release: verifies the attested native files, takes the conformance report of a plugin that declares
  sources from its job's artifact (exactly that one file, at most 256 KiB, nothing else), checks after every download
  that the staged tarball is the one the pack job kept (its sha256), writes `SHA256SUMS` and the notes (the version's CHANGELOG section), and shows them all in the run summary
  with the sha256 of `SHA256SUMS`.

A job either runs repository or dependency code (`npm ci`, the build, the pack stage, a host install) and has no write
token, or uses the API and runs only the kit's scripts on a fresh checkout, after checking that the release commit's
`scripts/` and `.github/` are the parent's. The first kind is not token-free: `actions/checkout` fetches with the job's
read-only (`contents: read`) token, and its post step and the artifact uploads run after repository code on the same
runner, so that code could reach a read-only token for this public repository and the runner's artifact token. Jobs
pass files as artifacts downloaded by the id the uploading job gave, and each is checked again on arrival.

After the approval, it downloads the staged artifact by the id the summary names, and refuses unless `SHA256SUMS` has
the sha256 the summary shows and every staged file matches it, the tarball is the one the pack job kept (its sha256),
every native file is the one the release commit's `manifest/native.json` pins, size and sha256, with each gzip holding
the pinned executable, and the conformance report is ok for this version. Then it checks everything again, creates the annotated tag
`v<version>` on the release commit (tagger `github-actions[bot]`, unsigned), checks the tag, creates the Release with the
notes, the tarball, the native files and `SHA256SUMS`, and deletes `release/v<version>`. The tag keeps the commit.

GitHub's signature and the bot identity show only that GitHub made the commit through its API for the workflow; anyone
with write access can make such a commit. What ties the release to `master` is its content: one parent CI passed, the
exact `package.json`, the allowed paths and the byte-for-byte rebuild. Never relax those because the commit is signed.

**A rejected, expired or failed run** leaves nothing behind: the `cleanup` job deletes `release/v<version>` when it points
at the parent or at that run's commit, and never touches another branch. No tag exists before the approval, so the
version is not burned: fix `master` and start again. If `cleanup` itself failed, the next run refuses until the branch
is deleted: `gh api -X DELETE repos/joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs/git/refs/heads/release/v<version>`.

**Resume.** If the run fails after creating the tag and before the Release is complete, start it again with the same `sha`. The plan finds the kit's tag on a release commit on that sha with no published Release, and resumes:
it makes no new commit, checks and installs the tagged commit, stages the files, and after a new approval reuses the tag
and adds what the Release lacks. Delete a draft Release a failed upload left first: the publish step refuses a draft.
Any other existing tag is refused: release the next version.

The repository's tag ruleset keeps a `v*` tag from being moved or deleted. A stray `v*` tag, one that never became a
Release, does not block later releases: only published Releases count, and drafts do not. Its version cannot be
released, so release the next one. To remove the tag anyway, an admin disables the `release tags` ruleset, deletes the
tag, and restores the ruleset exactly as it was.

**Known limit: a `v*` tag pushed by hand.** No ruleset limits who creates a `v*` tag, so anyone with write access can
push one by hand, pointing at any commit. Such a tag has no published Release, the forward-only check ignores it, and
Jelly installs only a published Release whose `SHA256SUMS` it verifies. But a user who installs
`github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<x>` directly gets whatever that tag points at. Only the release workflow makes
release tags; never push one by hand.

The release kit is these files, the same in every plugin: `scripts/release-rules.mjs`, `scripts/release-commit.mjs`,
`scripts/release-github.mjs`, `scripts/check-release-shape.mjs`, `scripts/changelog.mjs`, `scripts/release-version.mjs`,
`scripts/release-pack.mjs`, `scripts/publish-release.mjs`, `scripts/attach-native.mjs`, `scripts/native-manifest.mjs`,
`scripts/tested-hosts.mjs`, `scripts/check-release-plugin-add.sh`, `scripts/check-drift.mjs`, `scripts/capture-tools.mjs`,
`scripts/release-kit.test.mjs`, `scripts/drift-kit.test.mjs` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`. `scripts/check-copies.mjs`
pins each of the scripts whole by its sha256, so a plugin whose copy differs from the family's fails `npm run check`:
change the kit in every plugin at once, with the new hashes. Do not re-run the older `apply-release-kit.mjs`: it writes
back the kit that could release only `v0.0.0`.

Each release has its own tag, and a Git install does not update by itself. To move to a newer release, remove the old entry with `opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<old version>`, then add the new tag with `opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<version>`.

## Data handling

- **The OAuth token is OpenCode's.** The plugin never reads, stores, logs or prints it; the MCP transport and every
  refresh are OpenCode's. Nothing the plugin writes contains a token, an authorization code or a signed link's query.
- **Transcripts are other people's personal data.** `agents_get_conversation` returns a caller's words, the identifier
  your integration gave them, the phone number they called from, whatever the agent extracted, and the variables their
  app passed in. It lands in the model's context and in the session history on disk. There is no redaction: the point of
  reading a call is what was said. `conversations: "summary"` denies the words and keeps the metadata; `"off"` denies the
  history too. The match ignores case. `"off"` denies a name containing `conversation` or `transcript`, a name containing
  `call` and `recording`, and the shapes `get_call`, `list_calls` and `export_history`. It does not deny a generation or
  a transcription: those names do not match. `"summary"` denies the transcript tools and the transcript patterns.
- **Generated files stay on your disk.** `elevenlabs_save_media` writes under `mediaRoot` and returns a path, a size, a
  sha256 and, when the container states one, a duration. The bytes never enter the conversation, and nothing is
  uploaded anywhere.
- **The optional API key** is stored by OpenCode's credential store, is used for one read (`GET /v1/user/subscription`),
  and is never printed: not in status, not in an error, not in a log. Remove it in `/connect` at any time.
- **Nothing is sent anywhere else.** The plugin's only outbound requests are the media download you ask for and that
  subscription read; the doctor fetches ElevenLabs' own discovery documents. What the *model* sends to ElevenLabs is a
  separate matter: its tool calls go to ElevenLabs' own server, and one of those tools, `get_more_tools`, exists to
  carry a free-text sentence the model wrote itself. See Permissions below.
- **Redaction.** Text from OpenCode or the network is cut to one line, at most 160 characters, with URL credentials,
  queries and fragments removed and token shapes replaced, before it reaches status, the dialog or the session.

## Permissions

**Every tool is allowed by default.** With `access: "all"` an agent can, without asking:

- **Spend your credits.** Eighteen tools bill the workspace you signed in with: speech, images, video, image editing,
  generating inside a flow, running a flow's nodes, transcription, voice design, a sandbox command (billed by the
  second), placing a batch of phone calls or retrying one, running an agent's tests, generating an agent or a test with
  an LLM, indexing a knowledge-base document, running a RAG query, and building a brand kit from a website. Those whose
  description says neither way are counted as spending because each describes work ElevenLabs plausibly bills; silence
  is read against your money rather than for it. An image or
  video call returns **four variations by default** and speech returns **two takes**, so one call can be four billable
  generations, and asking for a retry starts and charges another. **Transcription bills too**, and it is a *change*,
  not a read: `access: "read-only"` denies it along with every other tool that can spend. Every paid result carries a
  cost line with the figure the result reported, or `Credits: not reported`. **No credit cap is set by default**, and
  then no estimate is sent before a paid call: the bounds are the workspace's balance at ElevenLabs and the permission rules (`ask-changes` asks
  for every paid call, `read-only` denies it, and a script's `ask` is refused). The caps (`sessionCreditCap`,
  `dailyCreditCap`) are opt-in; once set, the plugin asks ElevenLabs for an estimate of each paid call, reserves it
  before the call and bounds this plugin, not your account. Eleven of the eighteen have no estimate — every one but the
  seven that take `estimate_only` — so they run unpriced, and while a cap you set is on they are refused instead.
- **An estimate is a call of its own.** Without a cap the plugin sends none; one the model or a script asks for is theirs. It costs nothing — measured against a real workspace, two of them moved the
  balance by zero — but each one creates a flow and a node in the workspace. Under a cap, the plugin asks for one per set of
  arguments, keeps it for ten minutes, and sends it only where the paid call is permitted: the permission it asks for
  is the generation's own, never one of its own, and under `read-only` nothing is estimated because nothing may be
  generated. That permission is raised twice for one paid call — before the estimate and again for the generation — so
  under `ask-changes` expect up to two prompts. Earlier releases promised one; whether a host folds them has never been
  measured here.
- **What a cap cannot decide.** Exactly: **within one OpenCode the caps are exact; across OpenCodes a cap is crossed
  by at most one call's reservation for each one deciding before its read of the others' holds lands, so eight of them
  at 3,000 credits a call can spend 31,000 against a 10,000 cap; every OpenCode reads the store behind each call it
  admits and every five seconds besides, so none decides on a book older than that; a settled charge is never lost.**
  The crossing needs overlap: calls that wait for one another see one another, and those same eight, run one after the
  next, spend only the 9,000 that fits. A cap is not a
  lock: `ctx.storage` offers `get`, `set`, `remove` and `scan`, and no compare-and-set, so two OpenCodes running at once
  on one data directory each admit against what they have read. Nothing is lost to that race, because every hold and
  every charge has its own key that only its own OpenCode rewrites and a total is a scan and a sum, not a merge. The
  check and the hold are taken in memory with nothing awaited between them, so two calls in one process cannot both
  pass; the hold's key is then written and awaited before the call is dispatched, and a write that fails refuses the
  call. Set the caps with the bound you can afford to be crossed once per extra OpenCode, not as a hard limit on the
  account; the account's own limits are at ElevenLabs. A cap also binds one server entry: the `elevenlabs` entry this plugin manages. A second MCP
  entry pointing at ElevenLabs under another name serves its tools under that name's prefix, which this plugin's hooks
  never see, so its calls are priced by nothing here. `/elevenlabs-status` names such an entry when one exists.
- **Change live agents.** `agents_update` publishes straight to the branch it targets, `main` by default. It is not
  staged as a draft, and the plugin cannot undo it. A prompt edit changes what a production agent says to real callers on
  the next call. `agents_publish_draft` makes every change staged in a draft live at once.
- **Reach people outside this conversation.** `agents_submit_batch_call` has an agent **place real phone calls** to a
  list of recipients, and `agents_retry_batch_call` calls the failed and unanswered ones again; both spend credits.
  `agents_update_whatsapp_account` changes how an agent answers a WhatsApp number's users, and
  `agents_request_merge_proposal_review` notifies workspace members. None of these is a read: `ask-changes` asks before
  each, `read-only` denies them, and a script's call is refused whenever the rule would ask. The skills tell the model
  to confirm the recipients or the change with you first.
- **Store credentials in the workspace.** `agents_create_secret`, `agents_update_secret` and
  `agents_create_phone_number` store an API key, a secret or a Twilio or SIP credential, which ElevenLabs never returns.
- **Delete permanently.** `agents_delete`, `agents_delete_tool`, `agents_delete_phone_number` and
  `agents_bulk_delete_knowledge_base` cannot be reversed.
- **Publish and deploy.** `agents_create_deployment` moves live traffic; `agents_duplicate` and `agents_create_branch`
  create entities that can be deployed.
- **Grant access from outside.** `agents_get_signed_url` mints a signed URL that starts a conversation with a private
  agent, which ElevenLabs says to treat as a credential. `agents_get_link` returns an agent's existing shareable link,
  and `agents_get_conversation_audio_url` a 15-minute link to a call's recording; both are reads.
- **Read callers' calls.** Every transcript and its extracted fields, as above.
- **Send your audio to ElevenLabs.** The reference-file and asset-upload tools send what you point them at.
  `creative_transcribe_audio` does not: it takes no file and no path, and transcribes a node already on a flow in the
  workspace. No price in this plugin reads a file on this machine.
- **Write outside the project.** `elevenlabs_save_media` writes under `mediaRoot`. It asserts both its own action and
  OpenCode's `external_directory` rule for that folder before it fetches anything, so a session that denies
  `external_directory` writes nothing.
- **Ask ElevenLabs to build new tools, in words the model writes itself.** `get_more_tools` takes one free-text
  argument, `capability`, and ElevenLabs uses it to decide which tools get built next. It is the one tool that carries
  a sentence the model composed out of the workspace. It carries no workspace data, returns no tool and adds nothing at
  run time, but under `access: "all"` it goes out without a prompt. `ask-changes` asks for it; `read-only` denies it.
  ElevenLabs marks it read-only; this plugin declares it a change on purpose, to Jelly too, so a read-only helper is
  never given it.
- **Use a tool ElevenLabs adds later.** The `elevenlabs_*` rule allows it, and status names it as unknown. With no
  credit cap, the default, it runs unpriced. While a cap you set is on it cannot spend unpriced: a name this release
  does not classify is refused `PRICE_UNKNOWN` before it is sent, whatever it is called — the money gate is the tool
  table, not a name prefix. A new deleting tool still runs until it is classified,
  because permission is a separate axis from money: `ask-changes` and `read-only` are what bound it.

One line restricts all of it: set `"access": "ask-changes"` (reads run, everything else asks) or `"access": "read-only"`
(reads run, everything else is denied), or add a rule for one tool, such as
`{ "action": "elevenlabs_agents_delete", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }`.

In an unattended run such as `opencode run`, a tool that asks is refused rather than left waiting.

## Scripts

The tools RPC, `elevenlabs.tools`, lets a script call the same tools with no model, under the same spending guard. A
script runs as the agent of the session it names, so it gets the same default: with `access: "all"` it can make every
call above, spending credits included. To restrict a script, set `access` to `"ask-changes"` or `"read-only"`, or add a
rule to its agent or session. A script never waits on a prompt: an ask is refused, and a saved "Always allow" approval
does not authorize a script. [docs/scripting.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs/blob/HEAD/docs/scripting.md)
has the envelope and every refusal.

# Architecture

The plugin is a thin layer over ElevenLabs' hosted MCP server. OpenCode owns the MCP transport, OAuth, credentials,
permission prompts and tool output limits. The plugin registers the server, names its `/connect` entry, adds the default
permission rules, guards spending, saves generated files, reports status, ships three skills, and lets scripts call the
known tools through a tools RPC, and reads the workspace's conversations as a source contract source. It adds two tools of
its own and has no runtime dependencies: the source contract's modules are bundled in.
