## Setup

1. `parseOptions` validates the options; anything wrong fails with `OPTIONS_INVALID`.
2. `checkHost` compares `ctx.app.version` with `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`. Inside it the plugin starts; status calls only 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2 tested. Outside it, setup fails with `HOST_UNTESTED` unless `allowUntestedHost` is set.
3. The ledger is read from `ctx.storage` once, so the 24-hour total survives a reload.
4. `ctx.mcp.transform` registers `elevenlabs` at the selected region's URL, with `oauth.scope` pinned to seven scopes, or
   adopts the user's own entry at exactly that URL. Another region's URL is `stale`; any other is `conflict`.
5. `ctx.tool.transform` sets the namespace description and adds `elevenlabs_save_media`.
6. `ctx.agent.transform` inserts the default rules after each agent's base `* * allow`.
7. `ctx.integration.transform` adds the optional API key entry to `/connect`.
8. `ctx.skill.transform`, `ctx.command.transform` (`/elevenlabs-status`, `/elevenlabs-doctor`) and `ctx.rpc.register`
   (`elevenlabs/status`).
9. `registerToolsRpc` registers `elevenlabs.tools` with the spending guard's shapers.
10. `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")` prices a spending call from ElevenLabs' own estimate, may cut a `generations_count`
    the caller named to what the budget affords, and refuses a call that does not fit before it is sent.
    `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` charges the ledger and appends the cost line, and the expiry line for a
    generation's link. An `estimate_only` call is neither priced nor charged: its answer is remembered as the price of
    the paid call with the same arguments.
11. `watchIntegration` starts. Setup returns one cleanup that stops it, both hooks and the tools RPC.

Transforms are synchronous and never throw: a failure is kept as a problem for status, and cleared when the next replay
succeeds.

## Platform facts (OpenCode 2.2.3 to 2.3.2)

- **The sign-in is CIMD.** ElevenLabs' authorization server advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` and
  no registration endpoint, so OpenCode sends its own client metadata document
  (`https://opencode.ai/oauth/opencode/client.json`). Nothing ships with the plugin. A pinned `client_id` or
  `redirect_uri` would disable that; the plugin pins neither.
- **The scope pin.** OpenCode requests `oauth.scope` when it is set, otherwise the scope in the `401` challenge
  (ElevenLabs' names none), otherwise every scope in `scopes_supported`. ElevenLabs advertises eight; the plugin pins the
  seven its own MCP client asks for, so `ads_read` is never requested. A host test asserts the exact scopes in the
  authorization request and fails if the pin is removed.
- **Discovery.** The global MCP resource names `https://api.us.elevenlabs.io` as its authorization server, so the global
  and US servers share one. Each region serves the same documents with its own host, and each accepts CIMD.
- **The token never reaches the plugin.** OpenCode holds it and refreshes it; `/elevenlabs-status` sees only a
  credential's label. That is why the balance needs a separate key.
- **The hooks.** `execute.before` can change an MCP call's arguments on the model path and in Code Mode, and
  `execute.after` can add to a result. The tools RPC's executor bypasses both, so the same guard runs there through the
  block's own shapers.
- **Unattended Code Mode.** Up to 2.3.0 a schedule's `if: { code }` check runs once at creation, with asks settled
  unattended. From 2.3.1 `experimental.automation` replaces `experimental.schedule`: a code action's tools are
  authorized at creation the same way (an ask or a deny is refused), and the program runs, under an unattended grant
  for those tools, when the scheduler finds it due. Only a server process starts the scheduler; the host test starts it
  in its embedded host. The flag is `experimental.automations`, also read as `experimental.schedules`.
- **A plugin tool's declared permission only hides it on a deny.** Every plugin-owned tool that writes asserts its own
  action inside `execute`; `elevenlabs_save_media` does, on both paths.
- **Changing a server's URL changes its integration id** (`mcp_` + `sha1(name\0url)`), so a region change needs a new
  sign-in and leaves the old credential behind. A plugin cannot delete a stored credential (`ctx.credential` offers
  `activate` only), so `src/old-sign-ins.ts` computes the other regions' ids, asks `integration.connection.active` for
  each, registers any it finds in `/connect` as "ElevenLabs, old `<region>` sign-in (not in use)" so it can be signed
  out of there or with `opencode auth logout`, and status names it with that command.
- **`dist/tui.js` carries no zod and no host contract**: the RPC contract is plain JSON Schema, written with
  `Rpc.define`.

## The spending guard

**ElevenLabs is the only source of a price.** This plugin computes none of its own: no rate per character, per second
or per minute, and no measurement of a local file. A call that can spend is priced by sending ElevenLabs the same call
with `estimate_only: true` and the same arguments, and reading the figure out of its answer (`estimatePrice` in
`src/billing.ts`). `ESTIMATE_TOOLS` holds the seven tools whose live schema declares `estimate_only`; `SPEND_TOOLS`
holds the eighteen that can spend. A spending tool with no estimate — the eleven that are not in `ESTIMATE_TOOLS`,
from `creative_design_voice` and the batch calls to `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website` — has no price at all: with no cap it runs unpriced, and while a cap the owner set is on it is refused (`PRICE_UNKNOWN`).

**Caps are opt-in.** `sessionCreditCap` and `dailyCreditCap` default to `null`. With neither set, `quote` and
`quoteSync` send no estimate and refuse, clamp and reserve nothing. Each path records the figure the result itself
reports, or reports `Credits: not reported`. The script path keeps nothing between calls: with no call id on
`ShapeCall` it could not pair a result with its call, so it does not try, and it tells an `estimate_only` answer from a
paid result by the answer's own `estimate` object (`isEstimateResult`). Everything below about refusals, clamps, holds and the one-in-flight rule applies only while a cap is
set. The bounds without one are ElevenLabs' own balance check and the permission rules.

**The figure is read strictly.** `estimatedCreditsOf` reads `estimate.credits` first, because that is the field the
live result used (`{"estimate": {"credits": 761.5151418103446}}`), then the same five named keys settlement reads a
charge under, at the top level. Nothing is read out of prose, and nothing is walked for several levels: a figure this
parser does not find leaves the call with no price, which a cap, when set, turns into `PRICE_UNKNOWN`. The estimate sets the
reservation and, where no later figure is seen, the charge, so it is read under at least the rules a figure that could
*lower* a reservation is read under.

The figure ElevenLabs answers with is the **batch total** for the call it was sent, which live reconcile 1 measured: an
estimate for four images came back as 761.5151418103446 credits, about 190 each. It is often fractional, and a
fractional estimate is a real figure — the ledger rounds it up (`Math.ceil`) and the cost line names the figure it
rounded from. When the call states no count, the batch is the server's own default for that tool
(`GENERATION_DEFAULTS`: four for an image or an image edit, two for speech, one for a video), so a price divided per
generation is divided by that default and the cost line says so. A tool whose schema declares `generations_count` with
no default of its own — `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes` — gets no per-generation figure, only
the total.

**An estimate is free but not harmless.** Live reconcile 1 measured two of them against the workspace balance and saw
no movement and no new billable request, and each one created a flow and a node in the owner's workspace. So with no
cap the guard sends none at all, and under a cap it asks for one estimate per set of arguments, remembers the figure for ten minutes (`RESERVATION_MS`), and reuses it for
the paid call rather than creating a second flow. Different arguments are a different call and get their own estimate.

**The estimate is asked for only where the paid call could run.** `estimatorFor` asserts the paid tool's own permission
(`elevenlabs_<tool>`, through `ctx.permission.assert`) before it sends anything — never a permission of its own, so
nothing can be estimated that the generation itself may not do. Under `access: "ask-changes"` the estimate goes out
only if that permission is allowed, so an estimate never creates a flow for a generation the user is about to refuse.
Under `access: "read-only"` every spending tool is denied, the assert fails, and no estimate is sent either. A declined
or failed assert leaves the call with no price, which a cap, when set, turns into `PRICE_UNKNOWN`.

**How many prompts the user sees is the host's, and is not yet measured (RE-8).** Two asserts are raised for one priced
call: `estimatorFor`'s, before the estimate, and the generation's own when it runs. `test/unit/regressions-6.test.ts`
counts them, so the number cannot change unnoticed. Whether OpenCode turns two asserts into one prompt — by holding an
"allow once" answer for the same action within the same tool call — cannot be established without a host, and no
version of this plugin has measured it. Earlier releases of these docs said the user is "asked once"; that was a claim
about what a host does, written as though this plugin decided it. Live pass 2 counts the prompts under `ask-changes`.
The ordering itself is settled and is the safe one: asserting before estimating is what keeps `read-only` from creating
a flow, and what makes `ask-changes` refuse the estimate when the generation is refused.

While a cap the owner set is on, two kinds of call are priced or refused before dispatch: the ones the table classifies as
spending, and **any name the table does not classify at all, whatever it starts with**. There is no keyword list and
no prefix. A price that does not fit is refused (`SPEND_CAP_REACHED`), and a count the caller named is first cut to
what the budget affords; a call that named no count is refused at its whole figure rather than quietly given a smaller
batch than it asked for.

The unknown half is what closes the chain that starts at `get_more_tools`: a tool asks ElevenLabs to build more tools,
and a tool this release has never seen has no schema to check its arguments against and no `estimate_only` flag to
call, so nothing here could price it. A read the table already classifies still runs without a price, as it always
did, and so does the plugin's own `elevenlabs_save_media`.

Each refusal names what it could not price and what to do about it, in three shapes. A tool that takes `estimate_only`
is told to send the same call with `estimate_only: true` first. A classified spending tool that does not —
`creative_design_voice` and `agents_run_tests` — is told that ElevenLabs offers no estimate for it and that both caps
must be `null` to run it. A name the table does not know is told that nothing here can tell whether it spends, and to
set both caps to `null` or wait for a release that classifies it.

A price is **reserved** in the ledger before the call is sent and settled into a charge when its result arrives, so a
parallel turn cannot spend one budget twice. A call that fails, and a hold still open after ten minutes, is charged the
reserved price: the plugin cannot tell a free failure from a billed one. A later higher figure may replace that charge.
A zero or a missing result does not free the budget. A charge stays in the session that reserved it, whichever session
a later result is delivered under, exactly as it keeps that row's figure as its floor: a settlement may raise what a
call cost but never moves it to another session's budget. The ledger is append-only: every hold and every charge is one
`ctx.storage` key, `spend/<writerId>/<entryId>`, where `writerId` is unique to this plugin instance and only the
instance that created a key ever rewrites it. A total is a scan over `spend/` and a sum — there is no merge, no
`Math.max` and no read-modify-write of a shared record, so no writer can drop another's row. Pruning folds older
entries into that writer's own hourly key, `spend/<writerId>/h/<hour>`, and the hours of every writer are added
together, which cannot double-count because a charge is folded by exactly one writer. A folded hour is kept while any
minute of its hour is still inside the window, so a folded charge counts for up to an hour past its own day, and never
less than it. A key is removed only once it is past the window. Two ledgers handed one storage object share a book and
one daily cap, as two locations in one OpenCode do. Across processes, exactly: **within one OpenCode the caps are
exact; across OpenCodes a cap is crossed by at most one call's reservation for each one deciding before its read of the
others' holds lands, so eight of them at 3,000 credits a call can spend 31,000 against a 10,000 cap; every OpenCode
reads the store behind each call it admits and every five seconds besides, so none decides on a book older than that; a
settled charge is never lost.** The crossing needs overlap: calls that wait for one another see one another, and those
same eight, run one after the next, spend only the 9,000 that fits.

The bound follows from the order each path works in. `quote` can await, so it refreshes from the store and then
reserves: the most it can admit beyond a cap is one reservation for every OpenCode that read before the first of them
wrote. `quoteSync` cannot await before it dispatches, by the shaper contract, so it bounds its staleness behind itself
instead — it starts a read it does not wait for after the hold is taken, and the next call on that ledger decides from
a book that has seen the other OpenCodes' holds. A process that is idle, or whose calls all refuse, writes nothing and
would never read again, so setup also starts an unref'd timer that reads the store every `LEDGER_REFRESH_MS`, five
seconds, and stops when the plugin is disposed. Measured over one store, 100-credit calls against a 10,000 cap: two
OpenCodes spending together reach 10,000, eight reach 10,400, and an OpenCode that started before another spent the
whole cap admits one call before its next read, or none once the timer has run. Without those two reads the same
measurements were 20,000, 80,000 and a whole fresh cap. `reserve` keeps its check and its hold synchronous, with
nothing awaited between them, then
writes the hold's own key and awaits it before dispatch; a failed write takes the hold back out of memory and refuses
the call. Two machines share nothing. Two locations keep their own tools-RPC shapers. On the script path, one priced
call per session and method is in flight.

### What each tool is allowed to do

`classify()` puts each of the 237 live tools in one class: 100 reads, 1 export, 104 writes, 18 that can spend and 14
destructive. Nothing is left unclassified. The class is the worst thing a tool can do; it never decides whether a call
runs, only what the generated default rules give it.

**A read is exactly a tool ElevenLabs marks read-only.** The capture of 14 November 2026 records each tool's
`readOnlyHint`, and Jelly enforces the declared `readOnly` without loading the plugin, so the table follows the server,
with two exceptions kept stricter on purpose and named in `READ_ONLY_OVERRIDES`: `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag`,
which this plugin counts as spending (below), and `get_more_tools`, which sends the model's words to ElevenLabs.
`test/unit/live-tools.test.ts` fails on any other disagreement. ElevenLabs' `destructiveHint` is broader than this
table's `destructive` class: it also marks updates that replace a value (`agents_update`, `agents_update_settings`,
`agents_publish_draft` and others), which stay writes here; every delete is destructive, and ElevenLabs marks each one so.

**Five tools reach people outside the conversation** (`REACH_TOOLS`): `agents_submit_batch_call` and
`agents_retry_batch_call` place real phone calls, `agents_publish_draft` makes staged changes live to callers,
`agents_update_whatsapp_account` changes how an agent answers a WhatsApp number, and
`agents_request_merge_proposal_review` notifies workspace members. None is a read, so `ask-changes` asks before each,
a script's call is refused there because a script cannot answer, and `read-only` denies them. At the default `all`
they run, like every other tool; the two batch-call tools are also spending tools, so a cap refuses them.

Some of them are judgement calls, recorded here because nothing in the catalogue settles them. **One rule decides every
tool the catalogue is silent about:** a tool whose own description says it does server-side work ElevenLabs plausibly
bills, and does not say it spends nothing, is counted as spending. The tools that genuinely do not spend say so
unprompted — `creative_upload_flow_reference` ends *"This starts no generation and spends no credits"*,
`creative_update_node`, `creative_update_flow_nodes` and `creative_duplicate_flow_nodes` each end *"This never starts a
generation"*, `creative_get_voice_design_previews` says it reads previews *"without spending credits"* — so silence
beside billable work is the signal, and a cost line on a call that turns out free is better than a charge nobody
reported. These tools are classed as spending on that rule and nothing else; none of them declares `estimate_only`,
so each runs unpriced, or is refused while a cap is set, and live pass 2 measures whether they bill:

- **`agents_run_tests` and `agents_run_attached_tests`.** A test run makes the agent hold conversations, which bills
  the agent's own LLM usage. `agents_create_test`, `agents_create_simulation_test` and the other test tools only
  describe a test, and are ordinary writes.
- **`agents_generate` and `agents_generate_test_from_conversation`.** An LLM writes a whole agent, or a test from a
  real conversation, each taking up to two minutes.
- **`agents_compute_kb_rag_index`.** It starts RAG indexing of a knowledge-base document for an embedding model:
  embedding a whole document is server-side work with a unit ElevenLabs could bill.
- **`agents_query_knowledge_base_rag`.** A RAG query embeds the query and searches the index: the same kind of work
  `agents_compute_kb_rag_index` does. ElevenLabs marks it read-only; it is kept a change, because `access:
  "read-only"` promises to deny every tool that can spend.
- **`creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`.** It fetches a public website and extracts its logo, colours,
  typography and tone — *"best-effort and takes a while"*, which is the shape of a billed extraction.
- **`creative_design_voice` is counted as spending** and `creative_save_designed_voice` is a write: designing previews
  is the part that generates audio.
- **Three say they spend outright.** `creative_execute_sandbox` *"costs credits for each second the command runs"*,
  and `agents_submit_batch_call` and `agents_retry_batch_call` place real phone calls. `creative_get_sandbox_run`,

- **`creative_create_asset_upload` is a write, not an export.** It opens an upload into the workspace; nothing leaves

  read-only; they mint nothing, and they are reads now.
- **`creative_show_flow_results` is a read.** It puts a run's generations back in front of the user and changes nothing
  in the workspace, and ElevenLabs marks it read-only. An earlier release made it a write because rendering a view is
  an effect; the declaration now follows the server. It spends nothing and is not priced.

- **`get_more_tools` is a write, stricter than ElevenLabs' mark.** It is not a catalogue pager and it returns no tool definitions. Its live schema has
  one required argument, a free-text string named `capability`, and its description says what the server does with it:
  *"Call this when the user's request cannot be completed with any of the available tools. Describe the capability you
  were looking for, so it can inform which tools get built next."* So it changes what ElevenLabs will offer, which is a
  change like any other, and it is the one tool that sends words the model composed itself out of the workspace. It
  asks under `ask-changes`, `read-only` denies it, and SECURITY.md lists it with the other things `access: "all"`

  held it unclassified and described it as something it never was.

Nothing is left unclassified, so `/elevenlabs-status` reports `0 unknown` against this catalogue. A name that really
fits no class would go in `UNCLASSIFIED_TOOLS`, where `npm run drift` reports it as known rather than as drift — but
while a credit cap the owner set is on, a name the table does not classify is refused before dispatch, so holding one
there is not free.

### The one duration, and what it is not

`elevenlabs_save_media` prints how long a saved file is. Nothing else in the plugin reads a file's length, and no
price comes from one.

It used to. Until live reconcile 1 the guard priced a transcription by measuring the local WAV it was given, at a
per-minute rate written down here. The live catalogue ended that: `creative_transcribe_audio` takes no file and no
path — its arguments are now `connect_from`, `flow_id`, `model_id`, `view_state_id` and `estimate_only` — so
the audio it bills for is a node on a flow in the workspace, and the server never opens anything on this disk. A
duration measured here would have answered for a file ElevenLabs was not charging for. Transcription is now priced
the way every other spending call is, from ElevenLabs' own estimate, and the whole of the measuring apparatus the old
price rested on — the stamping of each file's device, inode, size and modification time before and after the
measurement, the freezing of the arguments that named them, the refusal of a file that moved between the two
readings — went with it. There is no local file in a price to protect.

What remains is `durationOf`, and it is a display figure. The saved line reads a PCM RIFF/WAVE file the way a decoder
does — the `fmt ` fields and the bytes behind `data` — and otherwise reads the duration an MP4 or M4A states in the
`mvhd` box inside its `moov`, which is the format ElevenLabs returns and carries no length a decoder-free reader
could compute. That walk is bounded: every read is inside the file's own size, the number of boxes it steps through
is capped, and a stated duration longer than the file's bytes could hold at 8 kbps is dropped rather than shown. A
file whose length depends on which decoder opens it — two `data` chunks, which CoreAudio and Python's `wave` read
differently, or two `fmt ` chunks, which are two sample rates and so two lengths — carries no duration on the saved
line at all. A `data` size that understates the bytes behind it is reported at the longer reading, with
`understated` saying so, so a line that disagrees with the owner's own player can be explained.

The rigour is kept because a figure shown to the owner should be one a decoder would agree with. It is not kept
because anything depends on it: `savedText` prints `Saved <mime> to <path> (<size>, <n> s).`, drops the seconds when
the file states none, and no cap, hold or charge reads that number.

# Configuration

Every option is optional. The plugin reads them from `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.9", "options": { "access": "all" } }] }
```

## Options

| Option | Values | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `access` | `"all"`, `"ask-changes"`, `"read-only"` | `"all"` | The permission posture the generated default rules express. |
| `region` | `"global"`, `"us"`, `"eu"`, `"in"`, `"sg"` | `"global"` | Which ElevenLabs environment's MCP server to register. Changing it needs a new sign-in; the earlier region's sign-in stays stored, and status names it with the command that removes it. |
| `sessionCreditCap` | a whole number of credits, or `null` | `null` (no cap) | Opt-in: the most one session may spend. |
| `dailyCreditCap` | a whole number of credits, or `null` | `null` (no cap) | Opt-in: the most this plugin may spend in a rolling 24 hours in this data directory, across sessions, scripts and restarts. Two machines do not share it. |
| `mediaRoot` | a path, `~` for your home folder | `"~/Downloads/elevenlabs"` | Where `elevenlabs_save_media` writes. Created on first use with mode 0700. |
| `maxMediaBytes` | a whole number of bytes | `209715200` (200 MB) | The largest file the save tool writes. |
| `conversations` | `"full"`, `"summary"`, `"off"` | `"full"` | How much of a call's history the conversation reads may return. |
| `allowUntestedHost` | `true`, `false` | `false` | Start on an OpenCode version outside `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`, with a note in status. |

Caps are opt-in. With neither set, the plugin refuses, cuts and queues nothing for money: ElevenLabs refuses a call the
workspace's balance cannot pay for, and the permission rules decide whether a paid call runs at all. `0` is refused for
either cap, because a typo in a cap you set must not be read as some other bound; leave the option out, or write `null`,
for no cap.

In Jelly, every option above except `mediaRoot` and `allowUntestedHost` is a setting, drawn with these values and
bounds. Jelly saves no `null`, so a cap there is no cap by being left unset.

## Spending

Eighteen tools can bill the workspace: `creative_generate_speech`, `creative_generate_image`,
`creative_generate_video`, `creative_edit_image`, `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes`,
`creative_transcribe_audio`, `creative_design_voice`, `creative_execute_sandbox`, `agents_submit_batch_call`,
`agents_retry_batch_call`, `agents_run_tests`, `agents_run_attached_tests`, `agents_generate`,
`agents_generate_test_from_conversation`, `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and
`creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`. A price is ElevenLabs' own figure: the same call with `estimate_only: true`.
There is no rate table in this plugin. Every paid result carries a cost line, with or without a cap.

The first seven take `estimate_only`. The other eleven do not, so with no cap they run unpriced, and while a cap you set
is on they are refused (`PRICE_UNKNOWN`). `creative_execute_sandbox` says it bills for each second its command runs, and
the two batch-call tools place real phone calls. The rest are counted as spending because ElevenLabs' catalogue says
neither way about them and they describe server-side work it plausibly bills — a test run's conversations, an LLM
writing an agent or a test, embedding a knowledge-base document, running a RAG query, reading a public website — and
the plugin counts silence against the owner's money rather than for it.

With no cap, no estimate is sent before a paid call: no flow or node is left in the workspace for it, and the call
raises no permission prompt beyond its own. It runs at whatever size it asks for, calls of one method run side by side,
and each is recorded at the figure its result reports, or its cost line says `Credits: not reported`. An explicit
`estimate_only` call still answers with ElevenLabs' figure, and is never reported as a charge.

While a cap you set is on, the plugin sends the estimate itself before each paid call.

While a cap you set is on, a priced call is clamped to the number of generations the caps afford, **reserved** in the
ledger before it is sent, and settled into a charge when its result arrives, so two calls that start together cannot
both spend the same budget. A failure is charged the reserved price. The daily cap is one total for this data
directory; two machines do not share it.

A call the plugin cannot price is refused with `PRICE_UNKNOWN` while a cap is on, never run unpriced: a failed or
missing estimate, an argument ElevenLabs' own schema for that tool does not have, any name the table does not know, and
the eleven spending tools ElevenLabs offers no estimate for — every one in the list above after
`creative_transcribe_audio`.

Under a cap, the estimate is sent only where the paid call could run, because it is a call of its own: it costs nothing, but it
creates a flow and a node in the workspace. Under `access: "ask-changes"` the permission you answer is the generation's
own, and nothing is estimated if you refuse. That permission is asked twice for one paid call — once before the
estimate, once for the generation — so you may see two prompts for it; whether OpenCode folds them into one is
OpenCode's to decide and this plugin has not measured it. The figure is then remembered for ten minutes, so the paid
call does not ask for a second one.

`access: "read-only"` denies every tool that can spend, `creative_transcribe_audio` included: a transcription runs on a
node in a flow, and billing a workspace is not a read.

## Files outside the project

`elevenlabs_save_media` writes under `mediaRoot`, which is outside the project, so **two rules** apply: the tool's own
permission (`elevenlabs_save_media`) and OpenCode's `external_directory` rule for the folder.

```json
{ "permissions": [
  { "action": "elevenlabs_save_media", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
  { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "/absolute/path/of/your/mediaRoot/*", "effect": "allow" }
] }
```

The second rule's resource is the **absolute** path of `mediaRoot` followed by `/*`; the default root is
`~/Downloads/elevenlabs`, and `~` is expanded to your home folder (the status report prints the expanded path). A refusal
whose message begins `permission.rejected: external_directory`, or that starts `EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY_DENIED`, needs that
rule; the plugin's own refusal prints the exact path to paste.

## Status

`/elevenlabs-status`, `/elevenlabs` and the status RPC print the same rows: `Connection`, `Account`, `Access`, `Region`,
`Spend`, `Conversations`, `Media`, `Skills`, `Tools`, `Agents without default rules`, `OpenCode`, `Next step`.

The `Region` row also names any sign-in OpenCode still stores for another region, which a change of `region` leaves
behind. OpenCode keys a server's sign-in by its name and URL, and a plugin cannot delete one, so the plugin lists it in
`/connect` as **ElevenLabs, old `<region>` sign-in (not in use)** and the status RPC reports it under `oldSignIns`, with
its integration id; when nothing else needs doing, the next step is `opencode auth logout <that id>`.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `connected` | signed in and the server lists tools |
| `sign-in required` | the stored credential needs a new sign-in: `/connect` → ElevenLabs |
| `connecting` | the server is still starting |
| `disabled` | the server is turned off in `/mcps` |
| `failed` | the connection failed; the row carries OpenCode's reason |
| `not configured` | OpenCode has no `elevenlabs` server, or yours points at another region's |
| `conflict` | your own `mcp.servers.elevenlabs` is at a URL that is not ElevenLabs' |

## Errors

Every code the plugin raises, in the order the table lists them:

| Code | What happened | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BALANCE_UNAVAILABLE` | The optional API key could not read the subscription. | Run `/elevenlabs-status`; if it keeps failing, remove the key in `/connect`. |
| `EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY_DENIED` | The save tool's `external_directory` rule is not allowed for the media folder. | Add `{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "<absolute mediaRoot>/*", "effect": "allow" }` to the agent's rules. |
| `HOST_UNTESTED` | OpenCode is outside `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`. | Use a supported OpenCode, or set `"allowUntestedHost": true`. |
| `MEDIA_EXPIRED` | The generated file's signed link has expired. | Fetch the generation again for a fresh link; do not generate again. |
| `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE` | The file is larger than `maxMediaBytes`. | Raise `maxMediaBytes` if you mean to keep a file this large. |
| `MEDIA_URL_INVALID` | The link is not `https`, carries credentials, or is not on ElevenLabs' generated-file host. | Pass the link a generation returned. |
| `OPTIONS_INVALID` | A plugin option is missing, of the wrong type, or out of range. | Fix the option; the message names the accepted values. |
| `PRICE_UNKNOWN` | A call that may spend cannot be priced, and a cap you set is on, so it was refused before it was sent. | Price it first with `"estimate_only": true` where the tool takes it, or set both caps to `null` — the refusal's next step says which. |
| `RULES_NOT_ADDED` | The default rules could not be inserted into the agents. | Restart OpenCode. |
| `SAVE_FAILED` | The file could not be written, or the folder changed while it was. | Check `mediaRoot`, its permissions, and the `external_directory` rule. |
| `SERVER_NOT_REGISTERED` | The MCP server could not be registered. | Restart OpenCode. |
| `SKILLS_INVALID` | A skill file is missing or malformed. | Reinstall the plugin. |
| `SPEND_CAP_REACHED` | The call would exceed the `sessionCreditCap` or `dailyCreditCap` you set, or, under that cap, a priced call of the same method is already in flight. | Raise the cap, set it to `null`, wait for the 24-hour window to roll, or wait for the in-flight call to return or for its ten-minute reservation to run out. |
| `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` | The status report could not be read. | Restart OpenCode, then run `/elevenlabs-status` again. |

An upstream error from ElevenLabs passes through unchanged, a `429` rate limit included: wait for the window it names.

`/elevenlabs-doctor` makes the checks a status report cannot: ElevenLabs' discovery document for the selected region, the

# Jelly

Jelly reads the `jelly` section of `package.json` without loading the plugin, so that section must describe the plugin
exactly. 239 tools are declared (101 read-only): the 237 ElevenLabs tools its server served on 14 November 2026, the
plugin's own `elevenlabs_save_media`, and the source contract's `elevenlabs_events_list`.
`test/fixtures/live-tools.json` is the capture of the 237, with ElevenLabs' own `readOnlyHint` for each tool, and
`test/unit/live-tools.test.ts` fails when the declaration and the capture disagree: a served tool left undeclared, a
declared tool the server no longer serves, or a `readOnly` that differs from the server's without a reason below.

Every declared effect is `allow`, because that is what the default rules give each tool in OpenCode at the default
`access: "all"`: every tool is allowed, and `access` is how a user restricts them. Jelly applies its own `access`
setting from each tool's declared `readOnly`: at **Allowed** every declared tool runs; at **Ask before changes** a tool
declared read-only runs and every other declared tool asks first; at **Read only** a tool declared read-only runs and
every other declared tool is denied. A read-only helper is never given a tool declared as not read-only.

Jelly's shared rules for every plugin of the family, word for word:

<!-- family-block:start -->
- At Allowed (`all`), the default, every tool runs without asking, declared or not, whatever its `effect`.
- At Ask before changes (`ask-changes`), a `readOnly` tool runs, and every other tool asks first, including a tool this plugin does not declare.
- At Read only (`read-only`), a `readOnly` tool runs, and every other tool is off, including a tool this plugin does not declare.
- A declared `effect` of `allow` changes nothing: the tool follows the access choice and its `readOnly`.
- A declared `effect` of `ask` makes the tool ask at Ask before changes, even when it is `readOnly`, and changes nothing at Allowed or Read only.
- A declared `effect` of `deny` turns the tool off at Ask before changes and at Read only, and changes nothing at Allowed.
- An action listed in `asks` asks first at Ask before changes and at Read only, and never at Allowed.
- A tool named with one `*`, such as another account's `plaud-*.get_file`, follows the same rules as a tool named in full.
- A choice the person makes for one tool wins over the access choice and the declared `effect`.
- jelly leaves out a key it does not know at the top level of the `jelly` block, and reads the rest.
- jelly refuses the plugin for a key it does not know inside anything it reads, such as a tool, a sign-in or a setting.
- jelly refuses the plugin, with one plain line, when `requires` names a field or a feature it does not read.
<!-- family-block:end -->

The declaration holds:

- `title`: `ElevenLabs`, and `summary`: one sentence on what the plugin reaches. The summary says what it touches; it
  states no policy, because what asks first is on the plugin's card.
- `icon`: `assets/icon.svg`, the mark Jelly draws. The same file names the one line in `jelly.summary`, and beside it the
  mark in `jelly.icon`.
- `cost`: the line Jelly shows on the plugin's review before it installs, in the plugin's own words, saying what it
  costs with ElevenLabs: "Eighteen tools spend the signed-in workspace's ElevenLabs credits, such as generating speech,
  images and video. A speech call renders two takes and an image call four by default, a retry is charged again, and
  each paid result has a cost line with the credits it reported. No cap unless you set one." It changes nothing Jelly
  allows.
- `tools`: the 237 ElevenLabs tools plus `elevenlabs_save_media` and `elevenlabs_events_list`, each with its permission
  action and `readOnly`. `readOnly` is true exactly where ElevenLabs marks the tool read-only, except for two that are
  declared stricter, as not read-only, so a read-only helper is never given them and `read-only` access denies them:
  - `elevenlabs_agents_query_knowledge_base_rag`: a RAG query embeds the query, work ElevenLabs plausibly bills, so
    this plugin counts it as spending; read-only access promises to deny every tool that can spend.
  - `elevenlabs_get_more_tools`: it sends the model's own free-text description of a missing capability to ElevenLabs,
    to decide which tools get built next. That is a message out of the workspace, not a read of it.

  `elevenlabs_save_media` is not read-only: it writes a file. `elevenlabs_events_list` is read-only: it lists the
  conversations' metadata through `agents_list_conversations`, `agents_list` and `agents_get`, and spends nothing.
  Five declared tools reach people
  outside the conversation, and none is read-only: `elevenlabs_agents_submit_batch_call` and `elevenlabs_agents_retry_batch_call`
  place real phone calls (and spend), `elevenlabs_agents_publish_draft` makes staged changes live to callers,
  `elevenlabs_agents_update_whatsapp_account` changes how an agent answers a WhatsApp number, and
  `elevenlabs_agents_request_merge_proposal_review` notifies workspace members.
- `skills`: `elevenlabs`, `elevenlabs-creative`, `elevenlabs-calls`.
- `signIns`: two.
  - `elevenlabs`, on the `elevenlabs` server, with `relay: {}`, which lets Jelly offer its relay to a browser tab that
    cannot reach the engine. ElevenLabs registers no clients and takes a client metadata document as the client id,
    which is what the relay needs, but the relay path has not yet been checked with ElevenLabs (README, Known limits).
  - `balance`, labelled **ElevenLabs API key (optional, balance only)**, on the plugin's own `elevenlabs-balance`
    integration, not required. It is the key `/connect` offers under the same name, used for one read, the workspace's
    credit balance in status, and never to generate.
- `rpc` and `views`: empty. `contributes`: no Home feed, widget or work kind, and six settings, each a top-level option
  of the same name with the parser's own values and bounds:
  - `access`: a choice of **Allowed** (`all`, the default), **Ask before changes** (`ask-changes`) and **Read only**
    (`read-only`), with Jelly's own line for each.
  - `region`: a choice of the five regions, `global` by default. Changing it needs a new sign-in: OpenCode keys the
    server's sign-in by its name and URL, so the card shows **Sign in again**. The earlier region's sign-in stays stored
    in OpenCode, because a plugin cannot delete one; the plugin lists it in `/connect` as "ElevenLabs, old `<region>`
    sign-in (not in use)" and status names it with the command that removes it.
  - `conversations`: a choice of `full` (the default), `summary` and `off`.
  - `sessionCreditCap` and `dailyCreditCap`: whole numbers from 1 to 10,000,000. Jelly saves no `null`, so a cap is no
    cap by being left unset, and neither declares a default.
  - `maxMediaBytes`: a whole number of at least 1024, 200 MB by default. The parser sets no ceiling, so neither does
    the declaration.

  Jelly draws each choice as a choice and each number with its bounds, and saves nothing outside them. A Jelly that
  does not know declared choices or bounds yet refuses the whole declaration. `mediaRoot` and `allowUntestedHost` are
  not declared: they are set in `opencode.json`.

**A tool ElevenLabs adds later is not asked about in Jelly at Allowed.** It is not declared, so Jelly knows only its
`elevenlabs_*` namespace: at **Allowed** it runs, a spending or deleting tool included; at **Ask before changes** the
namespace rule asks first; at **Read only** it is denied. Because it is not declared as not read-only, a read-only
helper is not fenced from it at **Allowed**. The way to bound it is the `access` setting or a rule in the agent's own
permissions; a credit cap, which is opt-in, refuses it unpriced while one is set.

Jelly treats an unknown key differently by level. At the top level of this section it drops the key and logs it, so a
misspelled top-level key is silent. Inside a tool, a sign-in or a `contributes` entry it refuses the key, and with it the
whole declaration, as it does for declared choices or bounds it does not know yet (above). That is why
`test/unit/jelly.test.ts` checks the declaration against the plugin's own rules and Jelly's authors' standard.

## A script runs as a session

Every call names a session, and the session must name an agent. Create it for the script once, with the agent the script
runs as, and keep its id (`data.id` in the reply). Give the project as the session's `location`: a session made without one belongs to the service's default location, where the project's agents may not exist, and each call then fails `Agent not found`. For example:

```sh
opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"call review","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"}}'
```

Never borrow a session found through history or a list: the script would run as that session's agent, under its rules.
The script then runs as that agent, with exactly the access its model would have:

- The rule for the tool's permission name, such as `elevenlabs_agents_list`, on resource `*` is resolved **before** the
  tool runs, in OpenCode's own order: the agent's rules, then the session's, the last match winning.
- **A script gets the same default as the model: every tool is allowed.** At the default `access: "all"`, the plugin's
  block allows every known tool and the `elevenlabs_*` namespace, so a script can read and change everything the account
  can, spend credits included. To restrict a script, set the plugin option `"access": "ask-changes"` (an ask is refused,
  because no one can answer a prompt for a script) or `"read-only"` (everything but the reads is denied), or give the
  script's agent or session a later rule. Only an `allow` runs; an `ask` and a `deny` are refused, with no tool call and
  no prompt left waiting. An agent defined only in your config gets no default rules; `/elevenlabs-status` names it.
- OpenCode then checks the call itself, as it does for the model: the agent's rules, the session's rules, then saved
  approvals.

**A saved "Always allow" approval does not authorize an ad-hoc script.** It lives outside the agent's and the session's
rules, so the resolve refuses an `ask` even after a past approval. That is deliberate: a script's permission must be
reviewable in config.

Session rules come after the agent's, so a session can narrow what its script may do. This one can read agents and
generate nothing:

```sh
opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"agent audit","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"},"permissions":[
  {"action":"elevenlabs_*","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"elevenlabs_agents_list","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"elevenlabs_agents_get","resource":"*","effect":"allow"}
]}'
```

## Calling a method

The body is `{"input": {"sessionID": "<session>", "input": <the tool's input>}}`. Both keys are required, and no other
key is allowed:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/agents_list -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{}}}'
```

The tool's input is ElevenLabs', and ElevenLabs defines its fields: `describe` shows each tool's schema as OpenCode lists
it now. Check it rather than guess a field name. ElevenLabs no longer takes the `context` argument earlier releases
passed: no live tool has it. Reading one conversation takes a `conversation_id` from a list result:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/agents_get_conversation -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{"conversation_id":"…"}}}'
```

`describe` takes nothing, or a session to resolve each method's permission for:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{}}'
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…"}}'
```

## Spending in a script

A script's calls count against the same rolling 24-hour ledger the model's do. Eighteen methods can spend, and every one
of them is a change: under `access: "read-only"` all eighteen are denied, `creative_transcribe_audio` included.

- **The price is ElevenLabs'.** It is the answer to the same call with `estimate_only: true`, which a script sends
  itself; under a cap the plugin needs one before each paid call. Seven of the eighteen take `estimate_only`; the other
  eleven — the batch calls, the sandbox, the test runs, agent and test generation, the knowledge-base index and query,
  `creative_design_voice` and `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website` — do not, so they run unpriced, and while a cap
  you set is on they are refused with `PRICE_UNKNOWN`.
- **No cap is set by default.** A script's paid call is then priced, refused, cut and queued for nothing: it runs at
  the size it asks for, two calls of one method run side by side, and each result's cost line states only the figure
  that result reports, or `Credits: not reported`. Nothing is kept between calls, so a call that failed leaves nothing a
  later result could be read against. An `estimate_only` answer is passed back as it is, with no cost line and no
  charge. Everything below about refusals, cuts, holds and in-flight calls applies only while a cap you set is on.
- **A script can ask for the estimate itself**, once, then call again with the same arguments. Under a cap, the plugin
  remembers the figure for ten minutes, prices the paid call with it, and does not create a second flow. An estimate costs nothing and returns no `cost` object, but
  it does create a flow and a node in the workspace.
- **The figure covers the whole batch.** It is for every generation the call asks for, not for one, it can be
  fractional, and it is rounded up to whole credits. Under a cap, a batch that does not fit is cut to what the budget
  affords; a call that named no `generations_count` is refused whole.
- Under a cap, a script's price is **reserved** before dispatch and settled when the result arrives, so two calls in flight cannot
  spend the same budget. A failed call is charged the reserved price. One priced call per session and method is in
  flight; a second, estimate or not, is refused until the first settles.
- **Only the arguments ElevenLabs' schema for that tool has may be sent while a cap is on.** One it does not have is
  refused `PRICE_UNKNOWN` by name, because nothing here can account for what it would change about the price.
- **A method this release does not know is refused while a cap is on**, whatever it is called. The RPC serves the
  methods in the table above, so this is about a tool ElevenLabs ships later: nothing here has its schema or its
  `estimate_only` flag, so nothing here can say whether it spends. Set both caps to `null` to run it unpriced, or wait
  for a release that classifies it.

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/creative_generate_image -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{"prompt":"a ceramic mug on marble","model_id":"gpt-image-2","generations_count":1,"estimate_only":true}}}'
```

Under a cap, a paid call with no price and no remembered estimate is refused `PRICE_UNKNOWN`, with no generation and
no charge, and a paid call whose price does not fit is refused `SPEND_CAP_REACHED`, also with no generation. Both refusals name the
option to change. Every paid result carries a `cost` object beside its output:

```json
{ "credits": 762, "basis": "exact", "sessionSpent": 762, "dailySpent": 762, "sessionCap": null, "dailyCap": null }
```

`basis` is `"exact"` when the figure is ElevenLabs' own estimate for exactly these arguments, which is every priced call
the plugin admits.

## Saving a file

`elevenlabs_save_media` is the plugin's own method, so its result is its own object rather than an MCP result:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/elevenlabs_save_media -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{"url":"https://…elevenlabsusercontent.com/…","name":"intro.mp3"}}}'
```

It answers `{ path, bytes, sha256, mime, durationSeconds? }`. It writes outside the project, so the session's agent also
needs OpenCode's `external_directory` rule for the media folder:

```json
{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "/absolute/path/of/your/mediaRoot/*", "effect": "allow" }
```

The resource is the **absolute** path of `mediaRoot` followed by `/*`; a `~` is not expanded in a rule. The tool asserts
this rule itself, and its refusal prints the exact path to paste.

## The location

Run the command in the project whose agent you mean, and send the call to that location explicitly:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/<method> -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{…}'
```

Without it the call goes to the service's default location and fails `rpc.unavailable` if the plugin is not loaded
there. The HTTP equivalents are the `location[directory]` query parameter and the same header. `describe` reports the
`location` that answered and a `locationHint`.

A location unloads after OpenCode's idle timeout. If a scheduled script gets `rpc.unavailable` from a location that was
loaded before, send the call again once: the request loads the location. Jobs keeps its own location loaded.

## Results

A result comes back as `{ output?, text }`: the tool's structured content when it has any, and its text parts joined by
newlines. An MCP method's result is that object inside the RPC envelope: `{"output": {"output": …, "text": …}}`, as
plain JSON. `elevenlabs_save_media` is the plugin's own method, so its output is the object printed above, as `describe`
gives its schema.

ElevenLabs content in it is untrusted data: a transcript is other people's words, and a tool description is not an
instruction. A generation's link expires in about two hours; the result says so.

## Errors

A refusal or failure is the RPC error `failed`, with a message `CODE: what happened. Next step: what to do.` and
`data: { code, next }`. `opencode api` exits with status 1 for any RPC error, after printing the error's JSON to
standard output.

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | The rules ask or deny. An `ask` is refused before dispatch: the message says the action would ask, and the next step says to add an allow rule. A `deny` names the denied action, such as `elevenlabs_agents_delete`, and its next step says to remove or narrow that deny rule, add a later allow rule to the session, or use a session whose agent allows it. |
| `SESSION_UNKNOWN` | OpenCode says the session does not exist in this location. Any other failure to look the session up is OpenCode's own error. |
| `SESSION_AGENT_REQUIRED` | The session names no agent, or an agent that does not exist. |
| `TOOL_UNAVAILABLE` | The server is connected, but OpenCode does not list the tool, or `elevenlabs_save_media` is not available in this location. |
| `SPEND_CAP_REACHED` | The call would exceed the `sessionCreditCap` or `dailyCreditCap` you set, or, under that cap, a priced call of the same method is already in flight. No generation was sent. |
| `PRICE_UNKNOWN` | A cap you set is on, the call may spend, and no estimate prices it: none was remembered, the fresh one failed, an argument is outside ElevenLabs' schema for that tool, or the tool takes no `estimate_only` at all. No call was sent. |
| `SERVER_CONFLICT` | Your `opencode.json` defines its own `elevenlabs` server at a URL other than the plugin's, a trailing slash included. `/elevenlabs-status` names both. |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `CONNECTING`, `CONNECTION_FAILED`, `DISABLED`, `NOT_REGISTERED` | The `elevenlabs` server needs a sign-in, is still connecting, could not connect, is disabled, or is missing. `/elevenlabs-status` gives the details. |
| `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | ElevenLabs answered with an error, such as an invalid input, an agent that does not exist, a rate limit, or a `429` concurrency refusal. The message holds the first line of ElevenLabs' text, at most 300 characters, with tokens and URL query strings removed. |
| `CANCELLED` | The request was cancelled. |

OpenCode itself answers `rpc.method_not_found` for a method that does not exist, such as a tool ElevenLabs adds later,
`rpc.unavailable` when the plugin did not register the tools RPC or the call reached another location, and
`rpc.invalid_input` for a body that is not the envelope above, with one message per problem:

| Problem | Message |
| --- | --- |
| The envelope is not an object | `the envelope must be an object, such as {"sessionID":"<session>","input":<the tool's input>}` |
| A key other than `sessionID` and `input` | `"extra" is not allowed`, naming the key |
| `sessionID` missing, not a string, or empty | `"sessionID" must be a non-empty string` |
| `input` missing | `"input" is missing` |
| `input` not an object | `"input" must be an object` |
| `describe` given anything but `{}`, a session or nothing | `describe takes nothing, or {"sessionID":"<session>"}` |

## The conversations source

The plugin declares one [source contract](https://github.com/we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract) source in
`package.json`'s `sources`, `elevenlabs.conversations`, read through two methods of this RPC beside the table above:

- `events_list` (action `elevenlabs_events_list`, also a tool): the conversations the workspace's agents had since a
  cursor, as normalised events, oldest first. Each event is metadata only: the conversation's id, its start, the agent
  as the one actor (`elevenlabs:<agent id>` and its name), a title of the agent's name with the call's direction,
  status and outcome (`Support Desk: inbound call, done, successful`), and the labels `status:`, `outcome:` and
  `direction:`. Its `text` is always empty and its `url` null: the callers are other people, so no caller, number,
  transcript, summary, score or feedback is ever in it, and ElevenLabs gives no link to a conversation. A conversation
  is listed once it is `done` or `failed`, or two hours after its start, so its outcome is known.
- `probe` (action `elevenlabs_probe`, a method only): who is signed in. ElevenLabs has no tool that names the account
  or the workspace, so the owner is OpenCode's sign-in for the `elevenlabs` server, `elevenlabs:credential:` and the
  credential's id, labelled with its label: a new sign-in is a new owner. It calls ElevenLabs for nothing.

`events_list` makes only free reads, which the descriptor's `permission.operations` names:

- `agents_list_conversations`: 100 at a time, oldest first, without transcript summaries; one to twenty calls a read,
  usually one.
- `agents_list` and `agents_get` (with `fields: ["platform_settings.privacy"]`), only when the read starts more than a
  day back and past any gap the cursor already answered: two `agents_list` calls (active and archived agents, one more
  per 100 agents) and one `agents_get` per agent, for each agent's retention.

Neither method spends credits, so the descriptor's `cost` is `free`, and both are allowed at every `access`. Any failed
call, or an entry that cannot be read, fails the whole read with its cursor held, so a page never drops one
conversation on its own.

ElevenLabs deletes an agent's conversations after its retention period, two years unless it is changed (its docs
disagree on whether the list row goes too; the source assumes it does). A read that starts before the latest horizon
among the agents (now less the shortest retention in days) answers `gap: {"reason":"expired","since":<its start>}` on
its first page only, then lists what survives. The cursor carries that gap for an hour, so a read that pages on answers
it once; a cursor used later is a new read, whose horizon is checked again. An agent with retention 0, or in Zero Retention Mode, keeps no
conversations by design: the source never sees them and answers no gap for them. A conversation a person deletes is not
seen either.
`conversations: "off"` denies `events_list` with the other reads of a call's history; one that runs anyway is refused
`SOURCE_DISABLED`. There is one account, `default`, which a call passes with its cursor.

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/events_list -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{"since":"2026-11-01T00:00:00Z","limit":50}}}'
```

The page holds the source, the account, the owner, the events, a `cursor` to pass back with `"account":"default"`, and
`more`. The cursor is the start and id of the last conversation listed, so it never expires. Its refusals carry the
contract's own codes:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INPUT_INVALID` | The input has an unknown key, a `limit` outside 1 to 500, a `since` that is not an ISO date or date-time, or a cursor without `"account":"default"`. |
| `SOURCE_UNKNOWN` | `source` is not `elevenlabs`. |
| `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH` | `account` is not `default`, or the cursor was issued for another sign-in than the one OpenCode holds now. |
| `CURSOR_INVALID` | The cursor was not issued by this source's `events_list`. Start again with `since`. |
| `NEEDS_SIGN_IN` | OpenCode holds no ElevenLabs sign-in, or the server needs one. |
| `SOURCE_DISABLED` | The `conversations` option is `"off"`. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | ElevenLabs refused the list for its rate limit. |
| `UNAVAILABLE` | The server is not connected or not ElevenLabs', a read failed, or ElevenLabs answered an entry or a retention it cannot read. Call again with the same cursor. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | A rule denies `elevenlabs_events_list`, `elevenlabs_probe`, or one of the three reads: `elevenlabs_agents_list_conversations`, `elevenlabs_agents_list`, `elevenlabs_agents_get`. |

## What scripts cannot do

- Call a tool that ElevenLabs adds later, even with an allow rule, until this plugin classifies it. Such a tool still
  runs for the model, under the `elevenlabs_*` rule; only the RPC needs it classified.
- Price anything without asking ElevenLabs first: this plugin publishes no rates, so a billed call is priced only by an
  estimate for exactly its arguments. Without one it runs unpriced, or, under a cap you set, it is refused.
- Rely on a past "Always allow": it does not authorize an ad-hoc script.
- Use a token: the plugin has none to give. The MCP connection, its sign-in and its refresh are OpenCode's.
- Keep a generated file without the `external_directory` rule, which is a path rule and not a permission on the tool.

A script's calls write nothing to the session, and OpenCode's `execute.before` and `execute.after` tool hooks, from any
plugin, do not run for them. The tools RPC applies the same spending guard itself, through its own shapers, so a script
is charged and capped exactly as a model's call is.
